local.name: FFTE
local.description: Discrete Fourier transforms in one, two and three dimensions, including serial and parallel variants.

classifications.notes: Documents complex FFTs and real/complex transforms; multidimensional coverage is recorded at J1 rather than treating every routine as one-dimensional.

The inspected ZFFT1D driver initializes twiddle tables with IOPT=0, factors supported lengths into powers of 2/3/5, and dispatches the complex FFT235 radix passes directly or through a blocked two-factor decomposition for larger vectors. IOPT=-1 selects the forward transform; IOPT=1 conjugates before the same FFT and conjugates/scales by 1/N afterward for the inverse. J1a2 records one-dimensional complex discrete Fourier transforms. The source requires N=2**p*3**q*5**r; FACTOR does not return an unsupported-factor error, so callers must validate the positive length themselves. B has 2*N complex entries and holds both scratch and coefficients. Large-path WX/WY tables are SAVE state: initialize again for the current length and do not assume independent large-length setups can be interleaved. Compiled param.h dimensions bound decomposition axes and no runtime bounds/status validation is supplied. Review covers the driver, factorization and radix dispatch, not every kernel, OpenMP behavior, MPI/GPU variants or numerical accuracy. No transform or round-trip was executed.

procedures.summary: External in-place complex-double FFT driver. A needs N entries, B needs 2*N entries; INTEGER N/IOPT must match the fixed-form build ABI. Initialize with IOPT=0, then use -1 forward or +1 inverse. Forward output is unscaled; inverse includes 1/N. Only positive 2/3/5-smooth lengths are supported, with additional compiled workspace-size constraints. There is no status dummy.
procedures.usage:
external :: zfft1d
integer, parameter :: n=8
complex(kind(0.0d0)) :: a(n), work(2*n)
a=cmplx(0.0d0,0.0d0,kind(0.0d0))
a(1)=cmplx(1.0d0,0.0d0,kind(0.0d0))
call zfft1d(a,n,0,work)
call zfft1d(a,n,-1,work)
! For this impulse the unscaled spectrum is all ones.
call zfft1d(a,n,1,work)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled small-path fragment. No spectrum or round-trip comparison was performed. Build/link zfft1d.f, fft235.f, kernel.f and factor.f with a consistent param.h include and compatible COMPLEX*16/default INTEGER conventions; the upstream test Makefile shows that source set and OpenMP flags. Retain the coefficient part of work between calls, reinitialize when changing length, and do not assume shared large-path tables are reentrant. The sample avoids unsupported prime factors and large decomposition dimensions.

procedures.summary: Counts powers of 2, 3 and 5 without returning a validation status for remaining prime factors.
Radix dispatch only reviewed; individual arithmetic kernels remain outside this audit.

local.name: Expokit
local.description: Matrix exponentials and exponential actions using dense approximations and sparse Krylov methods.

classifications.notes: Documents exp(t*A), exp(t*A)v and phi-function actions for dense and sparse matrices. Linear algebra is supported; a more specific matrix-function mapping awaits procedure review.

The inspected real dense DGPADM routine scales t*H, evaluates the diagonal Pade rational approximation using matrix products and a linear solve, then repeatedly squares the result. It returns the full exp(t*H) through an offset into caller workspace. D8 follows the published NAG GAMS convention grouping matrix functions with other matrix equations (the NAG D8 index lists real matrix exponentials); this is not a claim of a general Sylvester-equation solver. Only this dense real path is reviewed: sparse Krylov exponential actions, complex variants and phi-functions are not certified here. Invalid sizes, zero norm of t*H (including t=0 or H=0), and linear-solve failure STOP rather than returning a recoverable error. The caller must handle identity cases and provide valid positive dimensions and workspace. No matrix exponential, conditioning or scaling-extreme test was run.

procedures.summary: External double-precision dense matrix exponential. Use positive m, ldh >= m, recommended ideg=6, ipiv(m) and wsp length >= 4*m*m+ideg+1. exp(t*H) occupies wsp(iexph:iexph+m*m-1) in column-major order; iexph is one-based relative to the passed workspace. ns reports squarings. Handle t=0 or H=0 outside the routine because its zero-norm branch STOPs. Link compatible BLAS/LAPACK.
procedures.signature: CALL DGPADM(ideg, m, t, H, ldh, wsp, lwsp, ipiv, iexph, ns, iflag)
procedures.usage:
external :: dgpadm
integer, parameter :: m=2, ideg=6, lwsp=4*m*m+ideg+1
integer :: ipiv(m), iexph, ns, iflag
double precision :: h(m,m), work(lwsp), exponential(m,m)
h = 0.0d0
h(1,1) = 0.1d0
h(2,2) = 0.2d0
call dgpadm(ideg,m,1.0d0,h,m,work,lwsp,ipiv,iexph,ns,iflag)
if (iflag /= 0) error stop "matrix exponential failed"
exponential = reshape(work(iexph:iexph+m*m-1),[m,m])
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled calling sketch. The analytic reference is diag(exp(0.1),exp(0.2)), but no comparison was run. The result is the full matrix exponential, not entrywise exponentiation or just its action on a vector. Link ABI-compatible BLAS/LAPACK; some failures terminate inside DGPADM before the iflag check can run. The chosen nonzero matrix/time avoids its identity-case STOP.

local.name: FFTLog-f90
local.description: Logarithmically sampled Fourier-Bessel transform code, currently restricted to the sine-transform case.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly limits this version to mu=0.5 (the sine-transform case). This mapping does not claim a general-order Hankel transform implementation.

The inspected FFTL entry reweights logarithmically spaced samples, dispatches FHTQ and postscales using logarithmic spacing, bias, kr and rk. FHTI initializes FFTPACK and complex-Gamma transform coefficients. With mu=+1/2 or -1/2 this is the logarithmically sampled sine/cosine transform subset J1a3, not a conventional equally spaced FFT or a certified infinite-domain quadrature. FHTI setup can be reused only while N/mu/q/spacing/kr stay fixed. Its OK flag is not a full validation certificate (N<=0 can still reach OK=true), so validate positive N, nonzero spacing and positive kr/rk. The command-line driver restricts mu to +1/2 despite a cosine hint in an error message, and applies its own physical normalization. Lower-level FHTQ, FFTPACK and complex-Gamma arithmetic are outside this review. No transform, ringing or round-trip check was run.

procedures.summary: External REAL*8 setup. N/KROPT default INTEGER; MU/Q/DLNR/KR real double; KR may be adjusted. KROPT=1 selects quiet low-ringing adjustment. WSAVE needs 2*N+2*(N/2)+18 for Q=0, or 2*N+3*(N/2)+19 otherwise. Check logical OK and validate inputs independently.

External in-place transform of A(N). DIR=+1/-1 forward/backward; initialize WSAVE with FHTI first, using MU=+0.5 for sine or -0.5 for cosine. RK is r_center/k_center, not the product KR. Output uses the logarithmic grid and sqrt(2/pi) sine/cosine normalization documented here, distinct from the command-line driver extra scaling.
procedures.usage:
external :: fhti, fftl
integer, parameter :: n=16
integer :: i
logical :: ok
double precision :: a(n), work(4*n+19), kr, rk, spacing, r
kr=1.0d0
spacing=0.1d0
call fhti(n,0.5d0,0.0d0,spacing,kr,1,work,ok)
if (.not.ok) error stop "FFTLog setup failed"
rk=1.0d0/kr
do i=1,n
  r=exp((i-0.5d0*(n+1))*spacing)
  a(i)=exp(-r*r)
end do
call fftl(n,a,rk,1,work)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled interface fragment with r_center=1 and k_center=KR, so RK=1/KR after any setup adjustment. The short log range is illustrative, not an accuracy demonstration. Validate domain truncation, periodic-extension/ringing effects and grid/normalization before comparing transforms. Link FFTLOG plus bundled DRFFTI/DRFFTF/DRFFTB and CDGAMMA support. Never confuse RK ratio with KR product, or the library normalization with the CLI postprocessing.

local.name: adjac
local.description: Operator-overloaded automatic differentiation for sparse and dense real or complex Jacobians.

classifications.notes: The README documents AD types and Jacobian extraction. Its optional AD-aware FFT is not separately classified here.

The reviewed real adjac_double path records local first-derivative dependencies in module-wide tape arrays. Multiplication records the product rule through sum_taylor_a; get_dense_jacobian_a seeds dependent variables in blocks and traverses those dependencies backward to assemble Jacobian rows. adjac_set_independent seeds variable indices. This establishes operator-overloaded first differentiation, not higher derivatives or a numerical finite-difference method. The scoped review covers real variables and dense extraction; complex, sparse-COO, tapeless and FFT variants remain outside this source mapping. The shared storage and mode flag require coordinated lifecycle management and are not independently thread-local. Reset without product_mode preserves the previous mode. Fatal errors STOP rather than return status. No numerical derivative test was run.

procedures.summary: Reset shared tape indices before registering independent variables. Explicitly pass product_mode=.false. for the dense-Jacobian path; omitting it preserves the last mode. Existing AD values tied to an earlier tape must not be reused after resetting.

Public generic; inspected real vector overload takes type(adjac_double) x(:), double-precision xval(size(x)), and optional directional seeds dx. Dense mode numbers variables in x order. Scalar registration instead requires the variable index j.

Public generic; inspected real overload takes dependent type(adjac_double) y(:) as INOUT and a caller-sized double-precision matrix. Allocate one row per dependent and one column per registered independent; extraction requires tape mode. Specific get_dense_jacobian_a is private.
procedures.usage:
use adjac
type(adjac_double) :: x(2), y(1)
double precision :: jac(1,2)
call adjac_reset(product_mode=.false.)
call adjac_set_independent(x, [2.0d0, 3.0d0])
y(1) = x(1)*x(2)
call adjac_get_dense_jacobian(y, jac)
call adjac_free()
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch for the inspected real dense path, not a checked driver. The analytic expected Jacobian is [3,2], but this was not compiled or compared. Complete all extraction before freeing or resetting shared tape storage. The supplied author example demonstrates a separate complex-analytic specialization, which is not certified by this real-path source review.

procedures.summary: Release the shared tape arrays after all values and derivatives have been extracted. Existing tape-dependent AD variables become unusable; this does not reset the product-mode flag.

local.name: autodiff
local.description: Automatic differentiation supporting derivatives through fourth order.

classifications.notes: The short README states the fourth-derivative scope and a Make-based test command. Supported operators and numerical behavior await source review.

The inspected src/avd.f90 implementation propagates derivatives through overloaded products and elementary-function composition. The avd_d4 inheritance chain stores a value and first through fourth raw derivatives with respect to one scalar parameter; the product and Q4_f chain rules contain the corresponding binomial/composition coefficients. This is forward differentiation, not finite differencing or symbolic expression manipulation. CALL init() must populate the module function-pointer table before elementary functions are used. H1 is the differentiation leaf; there is no finer automatic-differentiation child in this taxonomy. The review covers the fourth-order product/exponential path, not every overload or the older root autodiff.f90 implementation. Source requests an eight-byte default REAL build; module and caller settings must agree. No author tests or derivative comparisons were executed.

procedures.summary: Public no-argument generic that initializes the shared elementary-function derivative table. Call before exp and other table-based elementary functions.

Public exponential generic, scoped here to the avd_d4 overload. Input/output contain v and d1..d4 in REAL(8). Seed an independent scalar with d1=1 and higher derivatives zero; extract the same fields from the result. These are raw derivatives, not factorial-scaled Taylor coefficients.
procedures.usage:
use AVD, only: avd_d4, init, exp
type(avd_d4) :: x, y
call init()
x%v=0.5d0
x%d1=1.0d0
x%d2=0.0d0
x%d3=0.0d0
x%d4=0.0d0
y=exp(x)
! Read y%v and y%d1 through y%d4.
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled fragment for the src/ implementation. Build module and caller with consistent eight-byte default REAL options as requested by the source. Initialization is shared module state; no concurrent-initialization behavior was checked. The linked author test exercises fourth-order arithmetic/trigonometric expressions, not this particular exponential fragment.

local.name: DNAD
local.description: Dual-number automatic differentiation for existing Fortran programs.

classifications.notes: Classification uses the documentation and quick-start guide embedded in dnad.F90. This is a review of that documentation, not a verification of every overloaded operation.

The dnadmod dual type carries a default-REAL value x and a derivative vector dx(ndv). Reviewed real assignment zeroes the vector, dual multiplication applies the product rule, and exp_d multiplies the seed vector by exp(x). The public entry is the exp generic; exp_d and mult_dd are private specifics. This is first-order forward automatic differentiation, with the derivative-vector length chosen at preprocessing time by ndv (default one), not a higher-order derivative or finite-difference implementation. Seed every derivative component explicitly for independent inputs and compile callers against the matching module. The header notes default single precision unless consistent compiler options promote default REAL. No derivative result was checked by execution.

procedures.summary: Public elemental exponential generic for type(dual). Read result%x for the value and result%dx for seeded first derivatives. Build dnad.F90 with preprocessing; -Dndv=N selects the number of stored directions. REAL assignment resets all derivative seeds to zero.
procedures.usage:
use dnadmod, only: dual, assignment(=), operator(*), exp
type(dual) :: x, y
x=0.5
x%dx=0.0
x%dx(1)=1.0
y=exp(x*x)
! Read y%x and y%dx(1).
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled fragment valid for ndv>=1. Compile the module with preprocessing and use matching default REAL settings in the caller. Other directions remain zero here. The derivative vector must be initialized; the type components have no default initialization. This is a different fork/interface from nickbrady/Fortran_DNAD.

local.name: Akima with Derivatives
local.description: One-dimensional Akima interpolation with derivatives with respect to arguments and input data.

classifications.notes: The README describes smoothing the absolute-value operation for data sensitivities. It explicitly cautions against substantial extrapolation.

setup forms segment slopes, extrapolated endpoint slopes and Akima weighted nodal slopes, then local cubic coefficients; interp selects an interval and evaluates its cubic. This establishes univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation. abs_smooth rounds the absolute-value weights when delta_x is positive, so that variant differs from unsmoothed Akima. The source assumes ordered distinct nodes and at least three points without checking them. Queries outside the data range continue the nearest end polynomial; this is not a reliable general extrapolation method. No shape-preservation, monotonicity or accuracy guarantee is inferred from the README, and no spline was run.

procedures.summary: External double-precision spline constructor. Supply n >= 3 strictly increasing abscissae and matching ordinates; allocate four coefficient vectors of length n-1. delta_x controls smoothing of slope-difference weights. No status argument or input validation is provided.
procedures.signature: CALL setup(n, xpt, ypt, p0, p1, p2, p3, delta_x)

procedures.summary: External evaluator returning values, argument derivatives and data sensitivities. All coefficient-sensitivity matrices are required, shaped (npt-1,npt); transpose the appropriate SETUP_DV direction blocks as the Python wrapper does. Output data sensitivities have shape (n,npt). Out-of-range queries use the nearest end polynomial.

local.name: fortran-rbf
local.description: Radial-basis-function interpolation and local derivative matrices.

classifications.notes: The rbf_mod source documentation identifies the RBF implementation, interpolation matrices and derivative matrices. Kept at interpolation class E pending a procedure-level review; no PDE solver claim is made.

The inspected rbf_type%build constructs a local RBF interpolation matrix for each caller-supplied neighbor stencil, obtains its inverse and forms derivative matrices from kernel evaluations. This is an interpolation service (E3), not a complete value-evaluation API: optional y is not referenced, and the routine neither fits data values nor returns values at arbitrary queries. The Gaussian unaugmented matrix path is identifiable in source; the derivative and polynomial branches need correction/checking. In particular, the Gaussian second derivative expression differs from the analytic derivative; polynomial-augmented B entries are not fully initialized before whole-matrix multiplication, and an active debug print indexes node ten without checking node count. Compile with USE_LAPACK: inverse_matrix has an empty alternative branch. Select a distance function first, validate indices and stencil nonsingularity, and use poly_order=-1 to avoid augmentation. No interpolant, derivative matrix or failure was checked by execution; no PDE-solver or general scattered-interpolator mapping is inferred.

procedures.summary: Type-bound rbf_type constructor, with x(num_dim,num_node), ngb_idx(num_ngb,num_node), a supported kernel selector and real(r8) parameter. r8 is hard-coded kind 8. ngb_idx contains valid one-based node indices; neighbor selection is caller work. Initialize distance_mod first. Reviewed unaugmented Gaussian use sets kernel_ga and poly_order=-1. Matrices are stored on the object; y is unused and no status is returned.

local.name: Fortran Davidson
local.description: Davidson and generalized Jacobi-Davidson algorithms for selected eigenpairs.

classifications.notes: The README describes DPR/GJD correction methods and an optional second matrix for generalized problems. Its stated suitability for diagonally dominant symmetric matrices is retained; broader robustness is not established.

The inspected dense ordinary-problem path projects a real symmetric matrix into a basis, dispatches DSYEV on the projected matrix, forms Ritz vectors/residuals, appends diagonal-preconditioned corrections and reorthogonalizes/restarts the basis. This mapping is restricted to METHOD=DPR with SECOND_MATRIX absent; generalized and matrix-free paths remain outside this review. The convergence check uses residual norms, despite argument prose describing eigenvalue error. HAS_CONVERGED flags remain true across iterations, so ALL(HAS_CONVERGED) need not mean all current residuals satisfy tolerance. DPR divides by eigenvalue-minus-diagonal without a near-zero safeguard. Initial basis has 2*LOWEST columns and expansion can exceed limits without robust shape validation. No numerical convergence or complete LAPACK/helper audit was performed.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine, despite its generalized name also solving ordinary real-symmetric problems when SECOND_MATRIX is omitted. Use numeric_kinds::DP, EIGENVALUES(LOWEST), EIGENVECTORS(N,LOWEST), METHOD, iteration budget, positive residual tolerance and integer ITERS. The interface has no success/status flag.
procedures.signature:
CALL generalized_eigensolver_dense(MATRIX, EIGENVALUES, EIGENVECTORS, &
     LOWEST, METHOD, MAX_ITERATIONS, TOLERANCE, ITERS, MAX_DIM_SUB, SECOND_MATRIX)
procedures.usage:
use numeric_kinds, only: dp
use davidson_dense, only: generalized_eigensolver_dense
! Initialize a real symmetric A(N,N), values(LOWEST), vectors(N,LOWEST).
! Choose valid subspace dimensions with room for the initial 2*LOWEST basis.
call generalized_eigensolver_dense(a,values,vectors,lowest,"DPR", &
     100,1.0e-8_dp,iters,max_dim_sub=max_subspace)
! Recompute every final norm(A*v(:,j)-values(j)*v(:,j)) independently.

local.name: chol-rev
local.description: Reverse-mode differentiation through a Cholesky factorization.

classifications.notes: The README documents the adjoint primitive that propagates factor sensitivities to the original positive-definite matrix. This is not classified as a general-purpose Cholesky solver or a complete automatic-differentiation system.

DPO2FT walks the lower Cholesky factor backward, propagating supplied factor adjoints through diagonal division, BLAS matrix/vector updates and diagonal halving. DPOFRT performs the corresponding blocked updates and delegates diagonal blocks to DPO2FT. This is a reverse first-derivative primitive for a scalar objective depending on an already-computed positive-definite Cholesky factor, not a factorization, solve or complete automatic-differentiation system. Only UPLO=L is implemented in the nonempty paths; the upper branches call XERBLA without reliably setting the advertised INFO=-8. Input checks omit LDC, so the caller must enforce it. The blocked path may overwrite entries above the selected triangle. Preserve the author triangular-adjoint convention when passing sensitivities onward. BLAS/LAPACK support routines and matching integer ABI are required. No adjoint identity or finite-difference comparison was run.

procedures.summary: External unblocked double-precision reverse primitive. A holds a valid lower Cholesky factor; C holds the lower factor sensitivities on entry and is overwritten with input-matrix sensitivities in the author triangular convention. Supply UPLO=L, N >= 0 and both leading dimensions >= MAX(1,N); check INFO. A and C must be separate valid arrays.
procedures.signature: CALL DPO2FT(UPLO, N, A, LDA, C, LDC, INFO)

procedures.summary: External blocked variant with the same double-precision input/output convention, lower-factor restriction and required leading dimensions. Calls DPO2FT for small problems and diagonal blocks. C is modified in place, including some upper entries; retain only the meaningful triangle. INFO is not an accuracy estimate.
procedures.signature: CALL DPOFRT(UPLO, N, A, LDA, C, LDC, INFO)
procedures.usage:
external :: dpofrt
double precision :: factor(2,2), adjoint(2,2)
integer :: info
factor = reshape([2.0d0,1.0d0,0.0d0,3.0d0],[2,2])
adjoint = 0.0d0
adjoint(1,1) = 1.0d0
adjoint(2,2) = 1.0d0
call dpofrt("L",2,factor,2,adjoint,2,info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "reverse Cholesky failed"
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled calling sketch. The supplied lower factor defines X=factor*transpose(factor); adjoint initially seeds the sum of the factor diagonal. Link these reverse routines with ABI-compatible BLAS and LAPACK support; this is not a standalone single-file program. The output uses the author triangular sensitivity representation, so do not automatically symmetrize or double off-diagonals without matching the subsequent contraction convention. No numerical check was performed.

local.name: NITSOL
local.description: Inexact Newton-Krylov methods for large nonlinear systems.

classifications.notes: The nitsol.f interface documentation describes backtracking, GMRES/BiCGSTAB/TFQMR and analytic or finite-difference Jacobian-vector products. Only interface documentation is reviewed, not convergence behavior.

The reviewed NITSOL path solves a square residual system with inexact Newton steps and residual-norm backtracking. The public driver validates option selections, partitions caller workspace and dispatches to nitdrv. The inspected GMRES path uses Jacobian-vector products, modified Gram-Schmidt and Krylov corrections; nitjv chooses supplied analytic products or directional finite differences and optional right preconditioning. nitbt evaluates trial residuals and reduces the step until its decrease condition holds. F2 is the system-of-equations leaf; the internal linear solves and residual norms do not make this a general nonlinear least-squares or optimization API. BiCGSTAB/TFQMR dispatch is present, but those implementations were not reviewed. Normal termination also permits a small-step criterion without the residual reaching ftol, so independently check the returned residual. Common blocks, saved initialization and the block-data defaults require coordinated builds and do not establish thread safety. No nonlinear solve or convergence test was run.

procedures.summary: External double-precision square-system solver. x(n) is the initial guess and returned iterate; f(n,xcur,fcur,rpar,ipar,itrmf) supplies the residual. jacv supplies selected J*v or right-preconditioner actions, or may be a dummy when both are disabled. Initialize the ten-element input array, provide info(6), parameter arrays and method-sized rwork, plus BLAS-compatible dot/norm callbacks. iterm=0 may mean small step rather than small residual; rwork(1:n) holds the final residual on the normal driver path.
procedures.signature: CALL nitsol(n, x, f, jacv, ftol, stptol, input, info, rwork, rpar, ipar, iterm, dinpr, dnorm)
procedures.usage:
external :: nitsol, residual, jacobian_action
double precision, external :: ddot, dnrm2
integer, parameter :: n=2, kd=2
integer :: options(10), info(6), ipar(1), iterm
double precision :: x(n), work(n*(kd+5)+kd*(kd+3)), rpar(1)
options = 0
options(4) = kd
x = [1.0d0,1.0d0]
rpar = 0.0d0
ipar = 0
call nitsol(n,x,residual,jacobian_action,1.0d-8,1.0d-10, &
            options,info,work,rpar,ipar,iterm,ddot,dnrm2)
! Check iterm and independently inspect work(1:n).
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled calling fragment for finite-difference, unpreconditioned GMRES. Supply an explicit residual implementation matching the documented callback and a linkable dummy jacobian_action (unused in these options). Link the complete NITSOL package including nitbd block data, required BLAS/LAPACK support and matching integer/double-precision ABI. GMRES workspace is n*(kd+5)+kd*(kd+3); different methods require different storage. No solution, residual or performance comparison was computed.

local.name: JFNK-Hookstep
local.description: Jacobian-free Newton-Krylov solution of nonlinear systems with a hookstep trust region.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly solves F(x)=0 using GMRES and a hookstep trust region. Its Lorenz example does not turn this mapping into general ODE time integration.

The inspected external newtonhook routine solves a square residual system using a matrix-vector callback, right-preconditioned GMRES and SVD-regularized hooksteps. It compares actual residual-norm reduction with the predicted reduction and retries trust-region radii. The author example approximates J*v by directional residual differences around module state new_x/new_fx; the core itself accepts a supplied operator and does not automatically differentiate an arbitrary callback. This is F2 root finding, not a general constrained optimizer or ODE integrator. Source limitations remain: newtonhook overwrites the GMRES return flag ginfo with the input print flag info immediately after the solve, so the advertised GMRES-failure propagation is not established; GMRES normalizes residual/Arnoldi vectors without explicit zero-norm guards. Some linear-algebra failures STOP. Reusing the saved Krylov state and module-wide solution arrays requires coordinated calls. No failure, periodic orbit or nonlinear accuracy result was reproduced.

procedures.summary: External routine using the separate module newton for saved state. Allocate new_x(n), new_fx(n), set new_x to the initial guess, then provide f(n,x,y), df(n,v,jv), in-place preconditioner dfp(n,v), parameterless monitor sub(), and double-precision dp(n,a,b). df must apply the Jacobian at the current shared iterate. info is both print-control input and termination output. Tolerances and trust-radius parameters are double precision; del=0 disables hooksteps.
procedures.signature: CALL newtonhook(f, df, dfp, sub, dp, m, n, gtol, tol, del, mndl, mxdl, nits, info)
procedures.usage:
use newton, only: new_x, new_fx
external :: newtonhook, residual, jacobian_action, precondition, monitor
double precision, external :: inner_product
integer :: info
allocate(new_x(2),new_fx(2))
new_x = [1.0d0,1.0d0]
info = 0
call newtonhook(residual,jacobian_action,precondition,monitor,inner_product, &
                2,2,1.0d-3,1.0d-8,1.0d0,1.0d-12,10.0d0,50,info)
! Check info and the independently evaluated residual at new_x.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling fragment only. Implement all callbacks; jacobian_action may use analytic products or the documented directional-difference template, precondition may be the identity and monitor may do nothing. Compile the source defining module newton before the caller and link GMRESm plus compatible LAPACK/BLAS. Choose m large enough for the Krylov solve; the author warns that restarting affects hookstep correctness. Module storage is shared. No system or claimed termination behavior was run.

local.name: ORTHPOL
local.description: Orthogonal-polynomial generation and Gauss-type quadrature rules.

classifications.notes: The brief README explicitly identifies orthogonal-polynomial and Gauss-type rule generation. No particular rule family, accuracy bound or integration API is inferred from the repository name.

The inspected DGAUSS routine constructs an n-point Gaussian rule from the monic orthogonal-polynomial recurrence coefficients. It builds the symmetric tridiagonal Jacobi matrix implicitly, iterates eigenvalues and first eigenvector components, sorts nodes and scales squared components by dbeta(1), the measure mass. It returns nodes and weights rather than invoking an integrand or returning an integral. H2c is therefore the precise quadrature-service mapping; an internal eigensolver does not make this a general eigensystem API. The caller must supply a valid positive integration measure and consistent recurrence coefficients. Negative beta entries and iteration exhaustion have error returns; eps is an eigensolver convergence parameter, not a requested integration-error bound. Other ORTHPOL recurrence-generation and Gauss-Radau/Lobatto routines are outside this source review. No moment or quadrature test was run.

procedures.summary: External double-precision Gaussian-rule constructor. dalpha(n), dbeta(n), dzero(n), dweigh(n), and workspace de(n) are required. dbeta(1) is the total mass; later entries are recurrence coefficients. Supply n >= 1 and positive deps. ierr=0 indicates normal return; -1/-2 flag size/negative beta and a positive value flags iteration exhaustion. Form the weighted sum yourself.
procedures.signature: CALL dgauss(n, dalpha, dbeta, deps, dzero, dweigh, ierr, de)
procedures.usage:
external :: dgauss
integer, parameter :: n=4
integer :: i, ierr
double precision :: alpha(n), beta(n), nodes(n), weights(n), work(n), q
alpha = 0.0d0
beta(1) = 2.0d0
do i=2,n
  beta(i) = dble(i-1)**2/(4.0d0*dble(i-1)**2-1.0d0)
end do
call dgauss(n,alpha,beta,epsilon(1.0d0),nodes,weights,ierr,work)
if (ierr /= 0) error stop "Gaussian rule failed"
q = sum(weights*nodes**6)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled calling sketch using the monic Legendre recurrence on [-1,1]. The analytic integral of x**6 is 2/7, but no moment comparison was run. The measure weight is already represented by the recurrence and quadrature weights: do not multiply it into the sampled integrand again. Rule-generation convergence does not bound integration error for a general function.

local.name: triasymq
local.description: High-order quadrature rules for triangles, squares, cubes and tetrahedra.

classifications.notes: The README lists supported geometric domains, symmetry variants, rule files and driver programs. Mapping is multidimensional quadrature; author drivers have not been executed here.

The inspected triasymq entry retrieves tabulated reference-triangle nodes and weights, expands the D3 symmetry and maps them affinely to caller-supplied vertices. trianmap rescales weights to the absolute triangle area. This is a fixed-rule service returning nodes/weights, not an adaptive integrand-callback interface. The supported requested polynomial degree is 1..50, distinct from the returned node count (up to 453 according to the table). The wrapper ignores its internal ier, so validate degree before calling and supply a nondegenerate triangle and adequately sized arrays. The internal explicit-shape quaequad dummy uses the incoming nptsout value before overwriting it: initialize numnodes to the supplied capacity rather than relying on the author driver uninitialized variable. Tables and expansion/mapping paths were inspected, but all rule moments, degrees and claimed extended-precision construction accuracy were not independently verified. Other domains in the repository are outside this source review.

procedures.summary: External REAL*8 triangle quadrature-rule retrieval. vert1,vert2,vert3 each have length two, rnodes has two rows and weights is a vector. Prevalidate degree n in 1..50 and nonzero area, allocate capacity at least 453 for the full range, and initialize numnodes to that capacity. On return use only entries 1:numnodes. No public error flag is returned.
procedures.signature: CALL triasymq(n, vert1, vert2, vert3, rnodes, weights, numnodes)
procedures.usage:
external :: triasymq
integer :: numnodes
double precision :: v1(2), v2(2), v3(2), nodes(2,453), weights(453), q
v1 = [0.0d0,0.0d0]
v2 = [1.0d0,0.0d0]
v3 = [0.0d0,1.0d0]
numnodes = 453
call triasymq(2,v1,v2,v3,nodes,weights,numnodes)
q = sum(weights(1:numnodes)*nodes(1,1:numnodes)**2)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled calling sketch for the unit right triangle. The analytic integral of x**2 is 1/12, but no numerical moment was checked. The weights already include triangle-area scaling. Degree two is the requested polynomial degree, not an allocation size. Prevalidate input because the public wrapper does not expose internal errors; this is not adaptive error-controlled integration.

local.name: hwode
local.description: CMake distribution of Hairer-Norsett-Wanner solvers for nonstiff, stiff, delay and differential-algebraic problems.

classifications.notes: The README enumerates DOPRI5, DOP853, ODEX, RETARD and RADAU variants. Individual solver classes and interfaces need separate source review before granular mappings are added.

DOPRI5 provides an explicit embedded Dormand-Prince 5(4) method for nonstiff initial-value systems. The inspected entry checks options/workspace, configures error tolerances and dispatches the stage/acceptance/step-control core in the same file. Stiffness detection can stop integration; it is not a stiff solver. This fork adds a LOGICAL DEBUG argument between IOUT and WORK, so an unmodified upstream DOPRI5 call is incompatible. Dense output requires selected component storage and SOLOUT configuration. Only this method, not all HWODE solvers, is source reviewed.

procedures.summary: External double-precision nonstiff ODE driver. FCN(N,X,Y,F,RPAR,IPAR) supplies derivatives. ITOL=0 uses scalar tolerances and ITOL=1 vectors. Y and X are advanced. With NRDENS dense components, the author allocates LWORK=8*N+5*NRDENS+21 and LIWORK=NRDENS+21.
procedures.signature:
CALL DOPRI5(N, FCN, X, Y, XEND, RTOL, ATOL, ITOL, &
     SOLOUT, IOUT, DEBUG, WORK, LWORK, IWORK, LIWORK, RPAR, IPAR, IDID)
procedures.usage:
! Initialize X/Y/XEND, tolerances, arrays and matching FCN/SOLOUT callbacks.
work = 0.0d0
iwork = 0
debug = .false.
iout = 0  ! no step-output callback; no dense components
call dopri5(n,fcn,x,y,xend,rtol,atol,0,solout,iout,debug, &
     work,size(work),iwork,size(iwork),rpar,ipar,idid)
if (idid < 0) error stop "DOPRI5 failed"
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use positive compatible tolerances and initialized callback parameters. IDID=1 reaches the endpoint; 2 means interrupted by SOLOUT. Negative codes describe input, step-budget, step-size and stiffness failures. The pinned example enables dense output; the fragment above disables it.

local.name: mtprng
local.description: Fortran 95 Mersenne Twister pseudorandom-number generator library.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the generator family and Fortran interface/build instructions. This does not establish statistical quality, stream independence or suitability for cryptography.

The inspected stateful MT19937 path seeds 624 words, twists and tempers 32-bit outputs carried in INT64 storage, and scales them by 2^-32 in mtprng_rand_real2 for intended [0,1) uniform output. It is not a 64-bit-payload generator despite the rand64 function name. Explicit mtprng_init is essential: default mti=-1 bypasses the outer mti>=624 block that encloses the proposed lazy-seed test, then indexes mt(-1). The default-state path is therefore unsafe. This review covers explicit positive single-seed initialization and real2 dispatch, not array seeding, range conversion, normal sampling or statistical/bitwise validation. No generator was run.

procedures.summary: Public single-seed initializer. Pass an INT32 seed and a state object; the initializer sets the word array and mti. Always initialize explicitly before drawing numbers.
procedures.usage:
use stdtypes, only: INT32, IEEE64
use mtprng, only: mtprng_state, mtprng_init, mtprng_rand_real2
type(mtprng_state) :: state
real(IEEE64) :: u
call mtprng_init(123_INT32, state)
u = mtprng_rand_real2(state)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Compile stdtypes before mtprng. The sketch uses an explicit positive seed and does not rely on the broken lazy-initialization branch. The source uses a long free-form line in seed initialization, so compiler line-length settings may be needed. Reproducibility, period and distribution quality have not been tested here; not for cryptography.

procedures.summary: Public REAL(IEEE64) uniform function, intended interval [0,1), advancing a previously initialized state. It scales the 32-bit integer-output path, not a full 53-bit real sampler.

The README documents complete/incomplete K/E/F integrals and sn/cn/dn functions plus author comparison data. Its extensive tests are useful future driver candidates but have not been run for this catalog.

The inspected public complete_elliptic_integrals wrapper returns complete first-/second-kind integrals. For 0<=m<1 it dispatches associated Fukushima integrals and forms K=B+D, E=B+(1-m)*D; m=1 has explicit infinite K/unit E, and m>1 uses reciprocal-parameter/complement transformations for complex outputs. Input is parameter m=k*k, unlike modulus-input libraries. Negative m returns NaNs and is not supported. C14 records elliptic-integral evaluation; public incomplete/Jacobi entries and full associated-integral arithmetic remain unreviewed. The build uses REAL128 internally even for REAL64 outputs. Exact equality/branch-cut, near-singular and extreme-parameter accuracy was not validated. This is a wrapper/transformation review, not a complete kernel audit or execution test.

procedures.summary: Public elemental elliptic-module subroutine. REAL(dp) parameter M; COMPLEX(dp) outputs FC (complete K) and EC (complete E). DP=REAL64; QP=REAL128 internally. local.name: gamma_f77
local.description: Quadruple-precision evaluation of the real Gamma function in Fortran 77.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly implements real Gamma using reciprocal-series expansion, recurrence and reflection. The mathematical discussion of complex Gamma is not taken as evidence of a complex-argument implementation.

The inspected GAMMA_MOD::TGAMMA evaluates real Gamma by a 48-coefficient reciprocal-Gamma expansion in Horner form, recurrence products after reducing |X|, and reflection for negative noninteger arguments of magnitude above one. Positive integer arguments take a factorial-product branch. C7a records Gamma evaluation; no log-Gamma, reciprocal-Gamma output API, incomplete Gamma or complex extension is inferred. QP=selected_real_kind(32) requires compiler support for at least 32 decimal digits and sufficient range for the source literal 1e4000. At zero/negative integer poles the routine returns that finite sentinel rather than an IEEE infinity or status. Default-INTEGER conversions of X are not range-guarded; NaN, infinities, overflow and large recurrence products are not handled robustly. The last DATA coefficient lacks the _QP suffix used by the others, so coefficient rounding deserves checking before asserting a full precision guarantee. gamma.f also contains a main test program after the module; extract/build the module separately when linking a different main. No accuracy or pole/overflow case was executed.

use GAMMA_MOD, only: QP, TGAMMA

x=0.5_QP
call TGAMMA(x,value)

local.name: modern_fftpack
local.description: Object-oriented Fortran modernization of NCAR FFTPACK 5.1.

classifications.notes: The README describes FFTPACK modernization and forward/inverse examples. Language-standard compliance and transform normalization are author claims awaiting independent checks.

The reviewed FFTpack type exposes public fft/ifft generics for in-place one-dimensional complex transforms. Each method determines N from the array, destroys/reallocates workspace, initializes factors/twiddle tables through CFFT1I, calls CFFT1F or CFFT1B and destroys workspace again. It is not a cached-plan interface. The low-level forward path reinterprets complex storage through ISO_C_BINDING and dispatches radix passes; the inspected terminal radix-four case scales by 1/(4*l1), consistent with the documented forward-normalized/inverse-unscaled convention. This differs from FFTE/FFTW-wrapper forward-unscaled conventions. J1a2 records complex 1D transforms, not all real, multidimensional or trigonometric variants. Supply a nonempty vector; workspace sizing uses log(N) and does not validate N>0 first. Errors may ERROR STOP instead of returning to the caller. Parent/submodule CFFT1F declarations differ in workspace INTENT attributes; compiler acceptance was not checked. Source review covers the wrapper, setup/dispatch and a normalization path, not all factorization/radix arithmetic, build portability or round-trip accuracy. No transform or author test was executed.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound generic, scoped to COMPLEX(wp) one-dimensional data, overwritten in place. wp is selected_real_kind(15,307) in this revision. A default-declared FFTpack object is sufficient; the method creates/initializes/releases workspaces itself. Forward normalization includes 1/N, unlike many FFT interfaces. Private complex_1d_forward is not the user entry point.

use fftpack_library, only: FFTpack, wp
type(FFTpack) :: transform
complex(wp) :: data(4)
data=cmplx(0.0_wp,0.0_wp,wp)
data(1)=cmplx(1.0_wp,0.0_wp,wp)
call transform%fft(data)
! Forward-normalized impulse spectrum is 0.25 in each bin.
call transform%ifft(data)

The high-level path repeats allocation and factor/table setup on every call, even with unchanged N. The constructor is not a reusable plan for these methods because create first destroys its workspaces. Errors can terminate execution. Parent/submodule workspace-INTENT differences and inherited numerical kernels need build/numerical checking before claiming portability or accuracy.

classifications.notes: The documented wrapper supplies generic and specific interfaces and requires an FFTW installation. Planned CMake support is not recorded as an available build system.

The inspected 1D COMPLEX(real64) dcfft1/dicfft1 bindings allocate FFTW-aligned complex storage, create an in-place FFTW_ESTIMATE plan, copy input after planning, execute the forward/backward FFTW call, copy output and destroy/free the plan/buffer. input(1)=cmplx(1.0_real64,0.0_real64,real64)

local.name: akima86
local.description: Akima 1986 univariate interpolation with a Python interface and Fortran implementation.

classifications.notes: The README cites the univariate interpolation algorithm and documents a gfortran-backed Python build. No assertion is made that the Python packaging exposes a standalone Fortran library interface.

The reviewed UVIPIA general path (ND>=5) locates successive intervals, estimates endpoint derivatives from weighted neighboring three-point slope estimates, forms cubic coefficients for NP<=3 or higher-degree basis factors, and evaluates the corresponding interval polynomial. This supports univariate piecewise-polynomial interpolation E1a, not a global polynomial, spline-system solve or smoothing fit. Ordered distinct XD is checked; invalid input prints a message and leaves YI at -9999 without a status argument. End extrapolation is linear, using endpoint slope estimates. The sketch uses NP=3 and ND=7; selecting larger NP does not establish higher-order derivative-estimate accuracy or shape preservation. Material findings: the general query loop unconditionally prints the OpenMP thread number and query index; the separate ND=4 cubic a3 formula repeats yuse(1) in its second term where the distinct second ordinate would be expected. That small-data branch requires checking/correction and is excluded from the sketch. No accuracy, small-data case or OpenMP execution was verified.

procedures.summary: External REAL(KIND=8) interpolation subroutine. NP, ND and NI are default INTEGER, XD/YD have length ND and XI/YI length NI. XD must be strictly increasing; XI can be unordered. The inspected general path requires ND>=5. NP<3 is promoted to three. Compile/link with OpenMP support because omp_lib and omp_get_thread_num are used even apart from directive handling. There is no success/status output.

external :: uvipia

xd=[(real(i-1,8),i=1,nd)]

local.name: Interpolation in 2D and 3D
local.description: Modernized interfaces to Renka scattered-data interpolation on planar, spherical and three-dimensional domains.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes srfpak, sphpak, qshep2d and qshep3d and their geometries. Gradient estimation is documented; the suite is not assigned a single univariate interpolation class.

The inspected quadratic_shepard_2d wrapper creates local quadratic models for scattered planar points through alg660::qshep2. The reviewed core builds weighted least-squares systems, applies Givens rotations and solves for nodal quadratic coefficients. qs2val blends those local polynomials with compact-support modified Shepard weights, returning the stored value exactly at a node; qs2grd differentiates that weighted quotient. E2b is scattered multivariate interpolation, not gridded tensor-product interpolation. Only this 2D path is reviewed: the spherical, triangulation and 3D variants are not certified here. The wrapper fixes neighbor counts, uses default REAL and requires at least six equal-length samples. Duplicate/collinear configurations and unsupported query locations have status paths. Query methods assume successful construction and do not guard against unallocated data. No interpolation or gradient check was run.

procedures.summary: Type-bound constructor for type(qshep_2d), using default REAL x(:), y(:), f(:), each of equal length >= 6. Values are incorporated into the stored fit. Type-bound default REAL value query at a planar point (px,py). Construct successfully first and check error_status after each query. If no nodal support covers the query, the core returns a NaN and the wrapper records code_outside_spanned; this is not a general extrapolator.

use quadratic_shepard_2d, only: qshep_2d

y = [0.,0.,0.,1.,1.,1.,2.,2.,2.]

call mesh%create_mesh(x,y,f)
call mesh%error_status(status)
if (status /= 0) error stop "mesh creation failed"
value = mesh%interpolate_point(0.5,0.5)
call mesh%error_status(status)

local.name: NdSpline
local.description: Multidimensional B-spline interpolation.

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies multidimensional B-spline interpolation and cites its mathematical reference. Boundary conditions, supported dimensions and derivative interfaces require further review.

The inspected spline object constructs tensor-product B-spline coefficients on Cartesian-product axes by solving one-dimensional basis systems successively, then evaluates target grids via basis matrices and BLAS products. Cox-de Boor recursion implements the basis, and the author 2D example concatenates x/y axes and flattens f(i,j) in Fortran order. This establishes gridded multivariate interpolation E2a, not scattered-data fitting. The basis order k means degree k-1 (k=4 is cubic). Supply valid strictly increasing axes and compatible sizes/orders. DGESV info is ignored in set_coefs_1d, so singular/invalid interpolation systems are not reported to the caller. Extrapolation is a saved module-wide flag shared across objects, not an object-specific setting; omitted init arguments retain its previous value. Reinitialization requires cleanup, and fin assumes initialized allocations. This review excludes skip_solve-only workflows and does not establish interpolation accuracy, extrapolation safety or derivative APIs. No author test was run.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound generic initializer for type(spline). ks(:) gives B-spline orders and ns(:) gives axis sizes; xs concatenates axes with length SUM(ns), and fs flattens the source grid with length PRODUCT(ns), first axis varying fastest. Use real64 arrays, at least two axes for this mapped scope, 1 <= ks <= ns, and valid distinct increasing axis coordinates. Set extrapolation explicitly; keep skip_solve false when evaluating data. Failures may STOP and no status is returned.
procedures.signature: CALL sp%init(ks, ns, xs, fs, extrapolation, skip_solve)

procedures.summary: Public type binding for a Cartesian-product query grid. ns(:) gives target axis sizes and xs concatenates target axes. Results are stored as the flat allocatable component sp%fs, not returned as an argument; reshape to the target shape in Fortran order. Read/copy sp%fs before fin. Use an initialized, fully solved object and queries inside the source domain; shape mismatches are not a recoverable status interface.

use NdSpline, only: spline, dp
type(spline) :: sp
real(dp) :: axis(3), values(3,3), result(1,1)
integer :: i,j
axis = [0.0_dp,1.0_dp,2.0_dp]
do j=1,3
  do i=1,3
    values(i,j) = axis(i)+axis(j)
  end do
end do
call sp%init([2,2],[3,3],[axis,axis],reshape(values,[9]), &
             extrapolation=.false.)
call sp%interpolate([1,1],[0.5_dp,1.5_dp])
result = reshape(sp%fs,[1,1])
call sp%fin()

local.name: PPR
local.description: Conservative piecewise polynomial reconstruction and remapping on one-dimensional structured grids.

classifications.notes: The README identifies ppr_1d, rcon1d and rmap1d with PCM/PLM/PPM/PQM and limiter variants. These are reconstruction/remapping components; their use inside transport examples is not treated as a general PDE solver.

The reviewed PCM path of ppr_1d reconstructs piecewise-constant cell profiles from cell means and remaps them by integrating profile/target-cell overlaps. rcon1d dispatches to pcm, which copies each cell mean as its constant coefficient; rmap1d/xmap1d selects that one-coefficient representation, and imap1d evaluates integral basis differences and divides the accumulated mass by target-cell width. A subsequent compensated-sum defect correction adjusts an extremal target mean. This establishes a degree-zero piecewise-polynomial reconstruction/remapping path in E1a; it is not point-sample interpolation or a standalone PDE integrator. Restrict this review to ndof=1, PCM, compatible monotone source/target edges over the same domain and positive cell widths. The higher-order PLM/PPM/PQM and limiter implementations were not fully reviewed. Workspaces and all option fields must be initialized; the init methods dereference opts even though declared optional. No conservation, positivity or remapping-accuracy test was run.

local.name: Cyclic banded matrix solvers
local.description: Solvers for cyclic tridiagonal and general cyclic banded systems.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes dctsv and dcbsv and their LAPACK/BLAS dependencies. Documented dependency-removal alternatives are not assumed to be enabled in every build.

The inspected serial DCTSV solves real square cyclic tridiagonal systems with multiple right-hand sides by paired endpoint elimination, small determinant solves for the even/odd terminal cases, and back substitution. DL(1) stores the top-right corner and DU(N) the bottom-left corner. Those corners make this a general real system rather than an ordinary tridiagonal matrix in the displayed ordering; D2a1 is used without implying a dense factorization. D/DL/DU are read-only and B is overwritten by solutions. N>=4 and leading-dimension checks precede work. No pivoting is implemented; exact-zero intermediate determinant checks do not prove singularity of the entire matrix, and INFO=0 is not a conditioning or accuracy certificate. The README recommends diagonal dominance and warns that error grows faster with N than LU. This review excludes general wider-band and OpenMP variants. No solve, residual or timing comparison was executed.

procedures.summary: External double-precision cyclic tridiagonal solver. Supply N>=4, NRHS>=0, DL(N), D(N), DU(N), and B(LDB,NRHS), with LDB>=N. The wrapped corner elements are part of DL/DU. B becomes the solution; diagonals are preserved. Check INFO, but also assess residuals independently. Link XERBLA (normally supplied by LAPACK).
procedures.signature: CALL DCTSV(N, NRHS, DL, D, DU, B, LDB, INFO)
procedures.usage:
external :: dctsv
integer :: info
double precision :: dl(4), d(4), du(4), rhs(4,1)
dl=-1.0d0
d=4.0d0
du=-1.0d0
rhs(:,1)=2.0d0
call dctsv(4,1,dl,d,du,rhs,4,info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "cyclic elimination failed"
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled fragment for a strictly diagonally dominant cyclic system with expected constant solution one. No residual was checked. Retain a copy of the original RHS for that check. This routine does not return reusable LU factors. Default INTEGER and double precision must match the linked error-handler ABI; positive INFO is an elimination-breakdown indication, not proof that every possible solver would fail.

classifications.notes: The separate external thomas routine performs forward elimination and backward substitution for an ordinary real tridiagonal system with k right-hand sides. The lower diagonal a(i) is read for i=2..n, the upper c(i) for i=1..n-1; a(1) and c(n) are unused. It overwrites b and d while returning solutions in z. This supports D2a2a (ordinary tridiagonal systems), not periodic corner coupling. There is no pivoting, dimension validation or error-status output, and division by zero or small elimination pivots is not guarded. Use appropriate nonzero-pivot inputs; no stability theorem or numerical check is established by this source inspection.

procedures.summary: External nonpivoted tridiagonal elimination. n and k are default INTEGER; a/b/c are double-precision length n arrays, d and z have shape (n,k). b and d are overwritten; a/c are declared INOUT but not changed in the inspected body. z receives the solution. There is no INFO argument.

double precision :: a(4), b(4), c(4), rhs(4,1), z(4,1)
a=-1.0d0
b=4.0d0
c=-1.0d0
rhs(:,1)=[3.0d0,2.0d0,2.0d0,3.0d0]
call thomas(a,b,c,rhs,z,4,1)

classifications.notes: The alpha-status README distinguishes implemented formulas from unchecked plans. Planned multidimensional Monte Carlo and acceleration methods are not classified as existing functionality.

The reviewed Newton-Cotes method evaluates a concrete integrand object at n+1 equally spaced nodes on a finite interval. init selects closed-rule weights for degrees 1..10, and integrate_1D performs a single fixed weighted sum without a tolerance or error estimate, supporting the nonautomatic callback quadrature leaf H2a1a2. LGL_nodes_weights constructs a requested-size Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto rule on [-1,1], using endpoint nodes and Jacobi-root iterations for the interior. Jacobi-root iterations stop after at most ten steps with no convergence status, and small-N and high-order behavior were not verified. classifications.notes: The README states the primal/dual LP forms and BLAS/LAPACK requirements. A complete LU factorization is used per iteration; the Delaunay driver does not establish a general-purpose interpolation library.

DUALSIMPLEX maximizes C-transpose*X subject to A*X<=B by applying revised simplex to the asymmetric dual. It accepts AT (the transpose), factors each basis with LAPACK, checks primal slacks/dual feasibility and switches from Dantzig to Bland pivoting when progress stalls. This is dense linear programming, not integer/global-nonlinear optimization or a numerical reliability certificate.

classifications.notes: The README documents the MultiNormalGenerator interface and rejects nonsymmetric or non-positive-definite covariance matrices. No behavior for singular covariance is claimed.

local.name: spherical_bessel_fortran
local.description: Spherical Bessel functions of the first kind for real and complex arguments.

classifications.notes: The README documents sbessj and zsbessj and discusses reliability limits near zeros and parameter extremes. Its reported digits of accuracy and author comparisons have not been reproduced here.

The inspected real SBESSJ evaluates spherical j_n(x), choosing a power series for |x|<=0.78*n and upward recurrence from sin(x)/x and (sin(x)/x-cos(x))/x otherwise. At x=0 the series returns j_0=1 and j_n=0 for n>0. C10a3 (real argument, real order) is used for the half-integer cylindrical-Bessel subset: j_n(x)=sqrt(pi/(2*x))*J_(n+1/2)(x) for positive x (NIST DLMF 10.47.3, https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.47.E3). The procedure exposes only nonnegative integer spherical n, not arbitrary real cylindrical orders, Y/Hankel or modified I/K functions. Negative order, a flagged low-accuracy positive-x region for n>50, and series nonconvergence print diagnostics and STOP. The low-accuracy guard uses x rather than abs(x), so negative-x reliability is not established by that guard. Series stopping uses an absolute term threshold and a finite 20+2*n budget; it supplies neither a returned error estimate nor a status code. Precision/accuracy claims in comments/README were not reproduced. Complex and quad variants and the comparison implementation remain outside this source review. No Bessel value or recurrence residual was executed.

local.name: Elliptic K via AGM

classifications.notes: The README defines K(k) with modulus k, lists supporting-module dependencies and describes precision variants. Optional real128 support depends on the compiler; parameter/modulus conventions must be respected in future drivers.

The inspected REAL64 elliptic_k overload evaluates the complete Legendre elliptic integral of the first kind with modulus k. It forms the complementary modulus as sqrt((1-k)*(1+k)); for k*k<0.5 it returns (pi/2)/AGM(1,k-prime), and otherwise uses an AGM/elliptic-nome logarithmic transformation. C14 is the elliptic-integrals leaf in this taxonomy; complete first-kind scope is recorded in the procedure rather than inventing a narrower code. IEEE branches return quiet NaN for NaN input or |k|>1 and positive infinity for |k|=1. Material limitation: although the interface advertises |k|<=1, the second branch calls arithmetic_geometric_mean_kernel(1,k), not AGM(1,abs(k)); negative k with k*k>=0.5 therefore reaches a signed-input dependency path and must not be assumed valid. The sketch uses nonnegative modulus and the simple direct branch. Dependencies are unpinned Git references in fpm.toml, and their full AGM/nome algorithms are outside this review. The committed module unconditionally imports/declares REAL128 as well as REAL32/64, so its build needs that kind despite README calling it optional. No integral or reference test was executed.

The public BILINEAR routine interpolates values from a regular rectangular input grid to query points using four tensor-product weights. It estimates uniform spacing from axis endpoints; it does not search nonuniform coordinates. DATA_IN is laid out (NY,NX) and POINTS is (NQUERY,2). The out-of-range branches contain CONTINUE rather than CYCLE, so they fall through to invalid indexing and overwrite the sentinel; upper endpoints are also unsafe. This mapping records implemented gridded interpolation, not correctness at boundaries or source review of the separate scattered-data/triangle methods.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine using default REAL. Require ascending uniformly spaced axes with at least two nodes each and strictly interior queries. The module imports other project modules and OMP_LIB, and prints elapsed time. The current out-of-domain handling is unsafe.

use interpolation, only: bilinear
real :: x(2), y(2), values(2,2), points(1,2), result(1)
x = [0.0,1.0]; y = [0.0,1.0]
values(:,1) = [0.0,2.0]
values(:,2) = [1.0,3.0]
points(1,:) = [0.25,0.5]
call bilinear(x,2,y,2,values,points,1,result)

local.name: polynomial_interpolation
local.description: Lagrange interpolation with derivative estimates and an interpolation-quality indicator.

classifications.notes: The README documents arbitrary data points and an auxiliary grid-to-grid interpolation routine. An error indicator is not described as a rigorously certified error bound.

poly_interp implements a Neville-style Lagrange correction recurrence for the polynomial through n+1 distinct samples, also propagating derivative corrections. It evaluates at zero, so callers shift their abscissae by the desired query. This is a single polynomial (E1b), distinct from the local moving-stencil grid wrapper. Output y(0) is the value and y(k) is derivative k, not divided Taylor coefficients. dy is the last signed interpolation correction, not a certified error bound. There is no input-validation/status interface; duplicate nodes divide by zero. Restrict this reviewed use to n >= 1 and 0 <= nd <= n: for n=0 or derivative orders beyond n, some dy entries need not be assigned. Accuracy, conditioning and behavior on closely spaced nodes were not checked by execution.

procedures.summary: External routine using selected_real_kind(12), named REAL64 locally. Pass xin(0:n), yin(0:n), output y(0:nd), dy(0:nd), degree n >= 1 and derivative limit 0 <= nd <= n. xin must contain distinct offsets from the target point, not absolute nodes unless querying zero. No error status is returned. dy entries are signed corrections, not guaranteed absolute errors.
procedures.signature: CALL poly_interp(y, dy, xin, yin, n, nd)
procedures.usage:
external :: poly_interp
integer, parameter :: rk=selected_real_kind(12)
real(rk) :: nodes(0:2), values(0:2), offsets(0:2), y(0:1), correction(0:1)
nodes = [0.0_rk,1.0_rk,2.0_rk]
values = nodes**2
offsets = nodes-0.5_rk
call poly_interp(y,correction,offsets,values,2,1)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled calling sketch. The analytic value/first derivative at 0.5 are 0.25 and 1, but no comparison was run. Match selected_real_kind(12) consistently with the external routine. A small final correction does not certify interpolation error, and duplicate or nearly coincident input abscissae need independent validation.

classifications.notes: The inspected ordered-grid branch of grid_interp selects a local n+1-point stencil for each target, shifts its abscissae to that target and calls poly_interp. Stencil changes produce a piecewise-polynomial interpolation scheme (E1a), without an established spline smoothness condition at transitions. Both values and requested derivatives are copied into the target matrix. The wrapper checks some sizes and rejects extrapolation outside a scale-dependent tolerance. The unordered-grid sorting path is present but outside this source review. Its reported dymax is updated as a maximum of signed dy values starting from zero, rather than absolute corrections, so negative corrections can be hidden; it is not an absolute error estimate. Use distinct strictly ordered samples, in-range ordered targets and 0 <= nd <= n. No grid interpolation or derivative error check was executed.

procedures.summary: External ordered-grid interpolation wrapper. n is local polynomial degree, nin >= n+1, nd is derivative limit, nout <= mxdout. xin(nin), fin(nin), xout(mxdout), fout(mxdout,0:nd), dymax(0:nd) use selected_real_kind(12). fout(:,0) stores values and later columns derivatives. Check ifail before using outputs; dymax has the signed-correction limitation. Link poly_interp, and also sort for the compiled unordered branch even when not used.
procedures.signature: CALL grid_interp(n, nd, nin, xin, fin, nout, xout, fout, dymax, ifail, mxdout)

external :: grid_interp
integer, parameter :: rk=selected_real_kind(12)
integer :: ifail
real(rk) :: nodes(4), values(4), queries(2), result(2,0:1), indicator(0:1)
nodes = [0.0_rk,1.0_rk,2.0_rk,3.0_rk]
values = nodes**2
queries = [0.5_rk,1.5_rk]
call grid_interp(2,1,4,nodes,values,2,queries,result,indicator,ifail,2)
if (ifail /= 0) error stop "grid interpolation failed"

local.name: spline_interpolation_fortran
local.description: Modernized Fortran spline routines originating with Rondall E. Jones.

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies the source lineage and Fortran 90 adaptation. Dimensionality, boundary options and derivative interfaces are left unclassified pending more detailed review.

SPLIFT assembles/factors a tridiagonal system for nodal second derivatives with user endpoint relations, solves it and recovers first derivatives; SPLINT locates intervals by hunt/bisection and evaluates cubic values/first/second derivatives. E1a records interpolating piecewise cubics, not smoothing. Use at least four strictly increasing nodes for the reviewed fit path. ISX=1 reuses the factorization only when nodes, workspace and endpoint coefficients are unchanged; validation is skipped on that reuse path. Success is IERR/KERR=1, not zero. SPLINT extrapolates the end cubic and returns KERR=2; equal adjacent nodes can STOP. N<4 fitting returns zero derivatives and IERR=2 rather than the normal cubic result. No interpolation, derivative or extrapolation accuracy was run; integration through SPLIQ is outside this mapping.

procedures.summary: External spline constructor. REAL(selected_real_kind(12)) arrays X/Y/YP/YPP length N, W(N,3), default-INTEGER N/IERR/ISX. ISX=0 first call. Endpoint relations are YPP(1)=A1*YPP(2)+B1 and YPP(N)=AN*YPP(N-1)+BN; all zeros give natural endpoints. Check IERR=1.

External evaluation of spline defined by X/Y/YPP. XI/YI/YPI/YPPI length NI; returns values and two derivatives. Queries may be unordered. KERR=1 normal, 2 extrapolation, 3 invalid NI. Preserve matching X/Y/YPP and check statuses before use.
procedures.usage:
integer, parameter :: rk=selected_real_kind(12), n=4
external :: splift, splint
integer :: ierr, kerr
real(rk) :: x(n), y(n), yp(n), ypp(n), w(n,3)
real(rk) :: xi(1), yi(1), d1(1), d2(1)
x=[0.0_rk,1.0_rk,2.0_rk,3.0_rk]
y=x
call splift(x,y,yp,ypp,n,w,ierr,0,0.0_rk,0.0_rk,0.0_rk,0.0_rk)
if (ierr /= 1) error stop "spline fit failed"
xi=1.5_rk
call splint(x,y,ypp,n,xi,yi,d1,d2,1,kerr)
if (kerr /= 1) error stop "spline evaluation not in range"
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled in-range linear-data fragment. Expected value 1.5, first derivative one and second derivative zero were not checked. Link both external routines with matching kinds; SPLIQ is not needed for this sketch. Only reuse W with ISX=1 when the documented node/boundary conditions are unchanged. No Numerical Recipes-derived search licensing/accuracy audit was performed.

local.name: SPRINT
local.description: Grid interpolation with bilinear interpolator interfaces and cached point weights.

classifications.notes: The inspected source interface identifies regular and curvilinear grids and cached weights. Periodic boundary handling is explicitly a TODO; source-interface inspection is not a full implementation or numerical review.

The inspected structured-grid path prepares four tensor-product bilinear weights from normalized x/y coordinates, caches them by a formatted coordinate key, and applies them to four supplied values. E2a records gridded bivariate interpolation; the type does not fetch a full field or perform three-/four-coordinate interpolation (higher-rank values carry extra fields). Important source defects prevent a general-use recommendation: REAL(8) regular-grid preparation uses FLOOR without the required one-based offset and leaves the fourth corner second index zero by writing corner 3 twice; REAL(4) uses CEILING but excludes the lower endpoint and accepts some cells past the final valid interval. apply calls prepare on a cache miss but computes its result only in the ELSE branch, leaving the first return undefined unless prepare is called explicitly. apply neither guards outside points nor checks value-array extents. Its corner order is (lower-left, lower-right, upper-right, upper-left) mapped to input positions (1,1),(2,1),(1,2),(2,2), not the usual rectangular-field order. The sketch is a restricted REAL(4), strictly interior, explicitly prepared interface illustration. Curvilinear location/inversion and dependencies are not audited. No interpolation or defect was reproduced by execution.

procedures.summary: Public generic type-bound initializer. Scope here is private REAL(4) one-dimensional-axis binding: x(nx), y(ny), optional default-INTEGER cache_size. It copies axes into REAL(8) storage and creates the cache. Regular axes must be increasing and equidistant, each with at least two points; no validation enforces this. Curvilinear overloads exist but are not the illustrated path.

Public generic for caching a point. The illustrated REAL(4) binding accepts scalar x/y and mutates the cache. Call explicitly before apply to avoid its unassigned first-return path. Boundary handling has documented defects, so the sketch uses a strictly interior point of a two-by-two grid.

Public generic, scoped to the REAL(4) scalar-field binding. Supply a two-by-two array in the source corner order: (1,1)=LL, (2,1)=LR, (1,2)=UR, (2,2)=UL, plus REAL(4) query coordinates. It mutates the cache; a prior prepare call is required for a defined return. Do not pass a conventional field slice without checking the swapped upper-corner ordering.
procedures.usage:
use bilinear_interpolator_mod, only: bilinear_interpolator_type
type(bilinear_interpolator_type) :: interp
real(4) :: x(2), y(2), corners(2,2), value
x=[0.0,1.0]
y=[0.0,1.0]
call interp%init(x,y)
call interp%prepare(0.25,0.5)
if (interp%is_outside(0.25,0.5)) error stop "point classified outside"
! Values of f=x+2*y in the SOURCE corner order, not normal field order.
corners(1,1)=0.0
corners(2,1)=1.0
corners(1,2)=3.0
corners(2,2)=2.0
value=interp%apply(corners,0.25,0.5)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled restricted fragment, not a checked or recommended general driver until the source defects are fixed. It assumes default REAL is kind 4, matches the REAL(4) overload explicitly and precomputes the cache. Expected value is 1.25; no comparison was performed. The author example instead needs external WRF data/projection dependencies and passes an ordinary rectangular slice, whose upper-corner order differs from apply. REAL(8) regular grids have separate indexing defects. Formatted coordinate keys use to_string(...,4) in a 30-character buffer; collision/rounding behavior and dependency implementation were not audited.

local.name: fortran_csr
local.description: Fortran compressed-sparse-row matrix construction and matrix-vector operations.

classifications.notes: The README supplies complex CSR examples and an optional MKL build flag. Matrix storage and multiplication are not treated as evidence of a sparse linear-system solver.

The public CSRcomplex%MATMUL binding checks the input-vector size and dispatches a complex CSR row sum, or MKL_ZCSRGEMV under the MKL preprocessor branch. The inspected fallback uses one-based ROW/COL arrays and sums VAL*X without conjugation. The type owns private storage and has public constructors/setters. Output Y is assumed-size and its capacity cannot be checked by the routine; dimension errors STOP the process. The separate NONZERO binding returns the terminal row pointer (NNZ+1), not NNZ, and setter allocation/search contracts are not fully verified. This review covers a valid constructed matrix and the non-MKL product path, not sparse solves, all insert/update behavior or MKL correctness/performance.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound subroutine on CSRcomplex. X(:) and Y(*) use COMPLEX(KIND=8); the square matrix dimension is stored privately. Caller must provide Y with at least SIZE(X) entries. Use A%MATMUL, not the private MATMUL_AXY or MATRIX_VECTOR_C names.
procedures.usage:
use csrmodule, only: CSRcomplex
type(CSRcomplex) :: a
complex(kind=8) :: x(2),y(2)
! Construct/populate a valid two-by-two A using the public constructor/set bindings.
! Initialize X and provide two output entries.
call a%matmul(x,y)
! Compare with an independently retained dense matrix product.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The fragment requires prior matrix construction and initialized X. KIND=8 is a numeric compiler kind choice; match the module build. Compile .F90 preprocessing with MKL disabled for the inspected fallback. Construction/growth and NONZERO counting need separate checks; no solver or benchmark claim is made.

local.name: PyIntegral
local.description: Fortran numerical integration of tabulated arrays and functions with Python interfaces.

classifications.notes: The reviewed README lists trapezoidal, Simpson and Gaussian methods. The repository formerly listed as IntegralALL now resolves to PyIntegral; the catalog uses the current canonical repository identity.

The external GAUSSLEGENDREQUADRATURE routine generates successive n-point Gauss-Legendre rules with polynomial recurrence/Newton root refinement, linearly interpolates tabulated X/Y at those nodes and returns the last weighted sum. This is nonautomatic finite-interval quadrature of gridded data, not a callback integrator or accuracy-controlled algorithm. N_INT is the last quadrature order, not a tolerance. Source finding: an optional-argument fallback computes N_INTERATIONS, but the actual loop uses N_INT directly; omitting it references an absent optional argument. Orders below one leave Z undefined. LININTERPOL status is ignored and its indexing is unsafe even for in-range queries: resetting its saved index to -1 can start the upward search at -2. The calling sketch does not repair this. The rule generator caps Newton refinement at ten steps without reporting nonconvergence. This review does not promote the larger INTEGRALALL dispatcher or every branch to source-reviewed.

procedures.summary: External subroutine using ModDataType::RP=8 and IB=4 numeric kind values. X/Y are arrays of N_VALUES samples, A/B endpoints and Z a scalar output. Always pass positive N_INT explicitly for this revision and keep all quadrature nodes strictly within a valid sorted input table. There is no returned status/error estimate.

use ModDataType, only: rp, ib

real(rp) :: x(3), y(3), value
x = [-1.0_rp,0.0_rp,2.0_rp]; y = 2.0_rp*x+1.0_rp
call GaussLegendreQuadrature(x,y,3_ib,value,0.0_rp,1.0_rp,10_ib)
! Analytic integral of 2*x+1 over [0,1] is 2.

local.name: generic_rk
local.description: Modular Runge-Kutta ODE integration with adaptive-timestep examples.

classifications.notes: The brief README describes modular ODE solvers and a Brusselator initial-value example. Method inventory, stiffness handling and error-control guarantees need source review.

The active rk_wrapper path selects the explicit seven-stage Dormand-Prince embedded tableau, then uses two weighted stage estimates for adaptive one-step integration of a callback-defined initial-value system. Tolerances are hard-coded to sqrt(machine epsilon), the estimator uses an L2 difference and a global maximum component scale, and accepted states use the bstar estimate. This records intended one-step nonstiff scope, not verified order or accuracy. A material source finding is that calc_k initializes dummy_y only once before the stage loop and accumulates all successive stage sums into it, instead of rebuilding each stage from y; the implemented stages therefore need correction/checking before relying on the named method. The first adaptive trial is not clipped to the interval endpoint; clipping occurs after a step. Rejection exhaustion STOPs; there is no status output. The routine writes to unit 22. Implicit/nonlinear-solver branches and their stiff suitability are not reviewed or mapped.

classifications.notes: The README documents direction-number initialization and strided generation. This is a deterministic low-discrepancy sequence, not a source of independent pseudorandom variates; no quadrature accuracy guarantee is inferred.

The inspected module constructs 31 direction numbers from user-supplied primitive-polynomial parameters, updates a coordinate by Gray-code XOR and lowest-zero-bit position, and supports direct-index Gray-code skip-ahead. use mod_sobseq, only: sobol_state
type(sobol_state) :: state
real :: u
call state%initialize(1, 0, [1])
u = state%next()

local.name: gfsolver
local.description: Hybrid Newton-bisection root finding for scalar functions.

classifications.notes: The brief README describes switching from basic Newton to a hybrid method after the iteration limit. Bracketing conditions, derivative callbacks and failure handling need further review.

The inspected module solves a scalar real equation through function-value and first-derivative subroutine callbacks; the dummy vectors have length one. sub_newton takes Newton steps and attempts a sign-changing bracket after its Newton iteration limit, then calls sub_hybrid_nb, which bisects when a Newton trial leaves its current interval. F1b describes general nonpolynomial scalar root finding; this is not polynomial root enumeration, a derivative-free interface or a square-system solver. The hybrid code updates the first endpoint when f(x)<0, so its input pair must have the matching sign orientation; it does not validate a bracket on entry. Failure paths print and STOP rather than returning a status, and the Newton path divides by df before testing for a small derivative. The optional fnorm on direct Newton success stores the residual computed before the final x update. The fallback call does not forward the optional tolerance or iteration controls, so the hybrid defaults apply there. Convergence, singular-derivative behavior and all bracket assumptions were not checked by execution.

procedures.summary: Public module Newton solver with hybrid fallback. fcn and dfcn are external subroutines called as (1,x,value), not scalar Fortran functions. xguess and x are REAL(ki) arrays of length one; tolerances, lower search limit, iteration count and fnorm are optional. ki is SELECTED_REAL_KIND(15,30).

CALL sub_newton(fcn, dfcn, xguess, x, minx_in, errrel_in, &
                errabs_in, max_iter_in, fnorm)
