use mod_gfsolver, only: ki, sub_newton
real(ki) :: xguess(1), x(1)
! Supply external callbacks fcn(n,x,f) and dfcn(n,x,df).
xguess = 1.0_ki
call sub_newton(fcn, dfcn, xguess, x)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; implement compatible explicit-shape/assumed-size callback vectors and declare the callbacks appropriately in the caller. A zero/small derivative may trigger a division fault or STOP; failures can terminate the calling program. Lower-bound randomization is not a general bounded-root guarantee. Optional controls are not forwarded to the fallback hybrid call. No program was compiled or run.

procedures.summary: Public module Newton-bisection solver. Supply a two-element REAL(ki) pair whose function values have the negative/positive orientation expected by the endpoint updates, along with both function and derivative subroutines. x is a one-element output array; optional tolerances and iteration controls have defaults.

The external CHOLESKY_FACTOR routine overwrites the lower triangle of a dense real matrix with a Cholesky factor by square-rooting pivots, scaling the column and applying rank-one trailing updates. The upper triangle is left as original input. This is the real symmetric positive-definite factorization scope, not a complete solve. The declared INTENT(OUT) ERROR is never assigned; it is undefined on return and cannot report failure. There is no positive-pivot/symmetry/size validation, so indefinite or zero-pivot inputs can produce invalid arithmetic and N=0 still references A(N,N). No numerical factorization or failure was reproduced; the catalog records an educational implementation with these limitations.

procedures.summary: External REAL*8 in-place lower Cholesky routine. A(N,N) must already be valid SPD and N positive. ERROR is an output dummy that is not assigned in this revision. The upper triangle is not part of the factor and must be ignored for reconstruction.

The reviewed CGL path generates Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto nodes mapped to [a,b], produces alternating barycentric weights with half endpoint weights, and evaluates a single univariate global Lagrange polynomial by the barycentric quotient. A near-node isclose test returns the stored sample rather than dividing by a small node difference. E1b records a single polynomial, not a piecewise interpolant or noisy-data fit. n is polynomial degree and arrays need n+1 elements despite some abbreviated shape comments. bary_weights only implements CGL weights, so the sketch does not combine it with CG/CGR nodes. Explicitly pass is_descending=.false.: the node generator default flag has declaration initialization and therefore retains a prior supplied value between calls. Positive n, distinct endpoints and adequate array extents are caller responsibilities; no error estimate/status is returned. Module imports require MKL BLAS95/F95_PRECISION even though this reviewed scalar interpolation path uses no BLAS operation. No interpolation result, extrapolation behavior or alternate node family was verified by execution.

procedures.summary: Public module node generator. For this review use tag="CGL", n>=1, REAL(rp) endpoints and xcol(0:n). rp is REAL64. Pass the optional logical ordering argument explicitly, because its internal initialized default is saved between calls.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine generating n+1 weights for CGL nodes, in the same ascending ordering as the sketch. n is the degree, not the number of elements. Supply a REAL(rp) array of length n+1; arbitrary nodes and CG/CGR weights are not implemented here.

Public module barycentric interpolation function. x, w and f each need n+1 REAL(rp) elements. Source documents ascending x. A query sufficiently close to a node returns its sample directly, using relative tolerance 1e-12 and absolute tolerance 1e-14. Otherwise the weighted numerator is divided by the weight sum.

use constants_m, only: rp

integer, parameter :: n=4

call cheb_node("CGL",-1.0_rp,1.0_rp,n,x,is_descending=.false.)
call bary_weights(n,w)
f=x*x
value=lag_intrp(n,x,w,f,0.25_rp)

Public TRAPECIO/SIMPSON generics dispatch to private precision-specific functions. The reviewed DP paths sort finite bounds, repeatedly halve trapezoid spacing (SIMPSON extrapolates (4*Tnew-Told)/3), stop on absolute change below EPS and restore reversed-bound signs. This is automatic finite-interval function quadrature, not a grid-only routine or general singular/infinite-interval guarantee. EPS defaults to 1e-2 and is an absolute successive-estimate test, not a rigorous error bound. MAXITER=26 is fixed; nonconvergence prints and STOPs the host process. Equal-zero estimates can cause early acceptance; no oscillatory-integrand or floating-point edge tests were run. Other Integration module algorithms and imported Linear routines remain outside this source review.

local.name: easydop853
local.description: Simplified subroutine interface to the explicit DOP853 ODE integrator.

classifications.notes: The README describes a simplification of Jacob Williams DOP853 interfaces. Users cannot set tolerances and other parameters through this simplified interface; complete configurability of the original is not claimed.

The inspected easydop853 wrapper initializes a DOP853 object and integrates a callback-defined initial-value system. The reviewed core evaluates explicit Runge-Kutta stages, scales embedded error estimates by absolute/relative tolerances, accepts or rejects steps and clips the last step to the requested endpoint. This is a one-step nonstiff method; stiffness detection is not a stiff solver. The wrapper fixes rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-24, nmax=2250000 and nstiff=1 and requests no output callback or dense output. It converts initialization and negative integration statuses into ERROR STOP rather than exposing a recoverable flag. It returns only the final x and y and exposes none of the configurable lower-level tolerance/statistics interface through its argument list. Local error control does not certify global accuracy. Other dense-output and event modes are outside this review. No orbit, decay test or error estimate was checked by execution.

procedures.summary: Module subroutine with real64 x as initial/final independent variable, real64 xend as requested endpoint, and an INOUT real64 state vector y(:). Callback fcn(me,x,y,f) must include class(dop853_class) me and assumed-shape state/derivative vectors, even if it does not use the object. Fixed tolerances cannot be changed through this interface. Failure ERROR STOPs; no idid is returned.

use easydop853_module, only: easydop853, deriv_func, wp
procedure(deriv_func) :: decay
real(wp) :: x, y(1)
x = 0.0_wp
y = 1.0_wp
call easydop853(decay,x,1.0_wp,y)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled calling fragment. Supply decay(me,x,y,f) matching deriv_func, with f=-y for the test equation; its analytic endpoint is exp(-1), but no comparison was run. Compile dop853_constants, dop853_module and easydop853_module in that order before the caller/callback. The wrapper returns only endpoint values; use the lower-level object interface if configurable tolerances, dense output, statistics or recoverable error handling are needed.

local.name: FORTRAN ODE Toolbox
local.description: Fixed-step and adaptive Runge-Kutta integration of first-order ODE systems.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the collection as work in progress and documents RK4/adaptive RK4. Advertised precision options and error control have not been reproduced in this catalog.

The inspected public fixed-step solver implements the classical four-stage explicit RK4 formula. The adaptive solver compares one full RK4 step with two half steps and accepts using an unscaled absolute maximum component difference, then adjusts the step with a fifth-root rule. Both solve a callback-defined first-order initial-value system. The fixed interface stores time/state by rows, whereas the adaptive output stores time/state by columns. The fixed routine does not guard a one-column solution buffer before dividing by n_steps-1; the adaptive routine requires a forward interval and a positive meaningful tolerance. Its discrepancy test is not a certified global error bound. I1a1a records one-step nonstiff scope. The separate VSS routine and stiff-system claims are not included in this review.

local.name: L-BFGS
local.description: Limited-memory quasi-Newton unconstrained optimization with a CMake build.

classifications.notes: The README identifies Nocedal limited-memory unconstrained optimization and repackaging with a C/C++ header. No bound-constrained capability or global-minimum guarantee is inferred.

The inspected LBFGS path constructs a limited-memory inverse-Hessian action from stored step/gradient-difference pairs, uses a More-Thuente-style MCSRCH line search and requests function/gradient values through reverse communication. The user supplies first derivatives, not a Hessian; G1b1b records smooth multivariate unconstrained minimization. DIAGCO optionally requests a positive diagonal scaling through IFLAG=2. The normal stopping test is ||G||/max(1,||X||)<=EPS after a completed line search; no global-optimality or local-minimum certificate is implied. The initial step is 1/||G|| before that test, so an exactly stationary starting point is not safely handled by this path. LBFGS and MCSRCH retain SAVE state and shared LB3 parameters; do not interleave independent solves as though this interface were reentrant. Preserve workspace and re-enter with the returned IFLAG. No minimization, gradient comparison or full audit of MCSTEP/BLAS dependencies was executed.

procedures.summary: External double-precision reverse-communication minimizer. N/M are positive default INTEGER; W needs N*(2*M+1)+2*M elements. Initially evaluate F/G and set IFLAG=0. Return 1 requests fresh F/G at X, 2 requests positive DIAG when DIAGCO is true, 0 reports normal completion and negative values report errors. Link the LB2 block-data defaults and keep the state/workspace intact between calls.
procedures.signature: CALL LBFGS(N, M, X, F, G, DIAGCO, DIAG, IPRINT, EPS, XTOL, W, IFLAG)
procedures.usage:
external :: lbfgs, lb2
integer, parameter :: n=2, m=3
integer :: iprint(2), iflag, calls
double precision :: x(n), g(n), diag(n), w(n*(2*m+1)+2*m)
double precision :: f, eps, xtol
logical :: diagco
x=[2.0d0,-1.0d0]
diagco=.false.
iprint=[-1,0]
eps=1.0d-8
xtol=epsilon(1.0d0)
iflag=0
do calls=1,1000
  f=0.5d0*sum(x*x)
  g=x
  call lbfgs(n,m,x,f,g,diagco,diag,iprint,eps,xtol,w,iflag)
  if (iflag <= 0) exit
  if (iflag /= 1) error stop "unexpected reverse-communication request"
end do
if (iflag /= 0) error stop "L-BFGS did not finish normally"
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled fragment minimizing a quadratic from an explicitly nonstationary initial point. It uses DIAGCO=false, so no diagonal-request branch is needed. The 1000-call guard is a caller limit, not a library convergence claim. Check an initially stationary point before entering this implementation. Link the complete lbfgs.f object, including LB2 and bundled support routines, with compatible default INTEGER/double precision; archive/block-data retention may require toolchain-specific handling. Saved/shared state prevents safe interleaving of solves.

procedures.summary: Block-data initialization of the shared LB3 parameters; not an additional callable minimization routine.

local.name: PCG Fortran
local.description: Fortran 2008 implementations of several PCG generator variants.

classifications.notes: The README enumerates supported state/output permutations and explicitly excludes variants requiring int128. Availability of the PCG family name does not imply that every PCG configuration is implemented.

The inspected oneseq 64-state/32-output XSH-RR branch initializes a fixed state, saves the old state, advances an LCG using multiplier 6364136223846793005 and increment 1442695040888963407, then xor-shifts/narrows/rotates the old state to an INT32 bit word. L6a21 records uniform pseudorandom word generation. Signed negative INT32 results are bit patterns, not failed draws; there is no real scaling or unbiased bounded-integer conversion in this binding. The arithmetic relies on compiler behavior for signed integer overflow and out-of-range narrowing, which Fortran does not portably define as unsigned modular arithmetic. Other PCG widths, stream families, output permutations, seeding and jump-ahead methods are outside this implementation review. The author C-comparison test was inspected but not run; no sequence or statistical quality claim is validated.

procedures.summary: Public inherited generic binding, shown only on pcg_state_oneseq_64_type: CALL takes an INT32 harvest output, updates the private INT64 state and emits a word from the previous state. local.name: Jacobi theta functions
local.description: Jacobi theta functions, generalized theta functions and logarithmic variants.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly uses a z convention with period one for theta3, unlike the NIST convention with period pi. Future comparisons must convert arguments consistently; no convention-independent identity is asserted.

THETA3 dispatches to a logarithmic implementation that shifts/inverts tau, reduces z, sums paired exponential terms and finally exponentiates the result. Source uses exp(i*pi*n*(tau*n+2*z)), so z has real period one, unlike conventions with period pi. Require Im(tau)>0. Invalid tau, excessive transformation/shift recursion and detected NaNs call EXIT(-1), terminating the process rather than returning status. MAXITER limits transformations/shifts, not the final series loop, whose stopping test uses floating-point stagnation. Only THETA3 and the inspected shared helper path are mapped here; the other advertised theta/log/generalized interfaces are not independently certified.

procedures.summary: Public scalar complex function. Z, TAU and result have kind KIND((1D0,1D0)); optional integer MAXITER controls recursion limits. Use the module interface so the optional argument is passed correctly. The private logarithmic helper is not a public entry.
procedures.usage:
use jacobitheta, only: theta3
integer, parameter :: dp=kind(1.0d0)
complex(dp) :: value
value = theta3(cmplx(0.0_dp,0.0_dp,dp), &
               cmplx(0.0_dp,1.0_dp,dp),maxiter=1000)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use finite inputs and positive imaginary TAU. Validate against the period-one defining series or an independent implementation with the argument conversion handled explicitly. The routine can terminate its host process; MAXITER does not bound the inner series. C interoperability of the separate BIND(C) log entries was not reviewed.

local.description: Reference Fortran numerical linear algebra library with BLAS and language interfaces.

classifications.notes: The README identifies the broad reference library and Make/CMake builds. This upstream repository is distinct from the selected perazz/fortran-lapack wrapper; individual routine mappings and build configurations remain to be reviewed here.

The inspected DGESV driver solves a general real dense square system with one or more right-hand sides. It checks dimensions, dispatches LU factorization with partial pivoting to DGETRF and solves through DGETRS only if factorization reports success. A is overwritten by LU factors and B by the solution; positive INFO reports an exactly zero pivot. D2a1 is the general-system class. This source review covers the driver interface and dispatch, not an audit of every BLAS/LAPACK kernel or vendor implementation. It does not establish conditioning, error bounds, inverse formation, sparse support or numerical accuracy by execution.

procedures.summary: External double-precision dense linear-system driver. A(LDA,N) is overwritten by factors, B(LDB,NRHS) by solutions, and IPIV(N) records row pivots. Check INFO before using the solution. Link a compatible LAPACK/BLAS library; this source file alone is insufficient.
procedures.signature: CALL DGESV(N, NRHS, A, LDA, IPIV, B, LDB, INFO)
procedures.usage:
external :: dgesv
integer :: ipiv(2), info
double precision :: a(2,2), b(2,1)
a = reshape([3.0d0, 1.0d0, 1.0d0, 2.0d0], [2,2])
b(:,1) = [9.0d0, 8.0d0]
call dgesv(2, 1, a, 2, ipiv, b, 2, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGESV failed"
! The solution is now in b(:,1).
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only, not a checked driver. Use a double-precision/integer ABI compatible with the linked LAPACK build; a vendor ILP64 build needs matching integer arguments. Preserve input copies if residuals or the original matrix are needed. INFO=0 is not a condition-number or accuracy estimate. No compilation, residual calculation or solver comparison was performed.

classifications.notes: The inspected real DGELS driver chooses QR or LQ factorization by matrix shape and applies orthogonal transformations and triangular solves for unconstrained least squares or minimum-norm underdetermined solves. For TRANS=N and M>=N, the reviewed path forms Q-transpose B and solves with R. The interface assumes full rank; positive INFO detects exactly zero triangular diagonals, not reliable numerical rank or near-singularity. D9a1 records the unconstrained L2 solution scope. Workspace queries and scaling are visible in the driver. This review does not certify all dependency kernels, rank-deficient methods, constrained least squares or runtime accuracy.

procedures.summary: External full-rank real least-squares/minimum-norm driver. TRANS selects A or its transpose. A and B are overwritten; B needs at least MAX(1,M,N) rows even when the input right-hand side is shorter. Query WORK with LWORK=-1 before allocating the working buffer, then check INFO after the solve.
procedures.signature: CALL DGELS(TRANS, M, N, NRHS, A, LDA, B, LDB, WORK, LWORK, INFO)
procedures.usage:
external :: dgels
integer :: info, lwork
double precision :: a(3,2), b(3,1), query(1)
double precision, allocatable :: work(:)
a(:,1) = 1.0d0
a(:,2) = [0.0d0, 1.0d0, 2.0d0]
b(:,1) = [1.0d0, 2.0d0, 2.0d0]
call dgels("N", 3, 2, 1, a, 3, b, 3, query, -1, info)
if (info /= 0) error stop "DGELS query failed"
lwork = max(1, ceiling(query(1)))
allocate(work(lwork))

classifications.notes: The source interface includes differentiation of a supplied Jacobian and explicitly selects real128. Interface inspection does not establish supported platforms, stencil accuracy or successful compilation; real128 availability is compiler-dependent.

The inspected findiff and findiff_multiscale paths perturb each coordinate and combine symmetric 3-, 5-, 7- or 9-point stencils to approximate a square vector-function Jacobian. findiffhes instead differences a supplied square Jacobian callback and returns a rank-three derivative tensor; it does not directly compute a scalar Hessian from scalar function values. All reviewed interfaces use iso_fortran_env real128, require nonzero suitable perturbations and provide no automatic step selection, error estimate or status. The author test files select real64 while the module selects real128 and need consistent kinds/imports before they can serve as drivers. The matrix-in-time and multiscale-tensor paths are not included in this review. No stencil error or compilation failure was reproduced.

SETULB partitions workspace and dispatches MAINLB. This is smooth simple-bound optimization with caller-supplied first derivatives, not general nonlinear constraints or a global optimum guarantee. CALL SETULB(N, M, X, L, U, NBD, F, G, FACTR, PGTOL, WA, IWA, &
     TASK, IPRINT, CSAVE, LSAVE, ISAVE, DSAVE)

! Declare/allocate the documented workspace and initialize X, bounds and NBD.
task = "START"
do
  call setulb(n,m,x,l,u,nbd,f,g,factr,pgtol,wa,iwa, &
       task,iprint,csave,lsave,isave,dsave)
  if (task(1:2) == "FG") then
    ! Evaluate both F and G at the returned X here.
  else if (task(1:5) == "NEW_X") then
    cycle
  else
    exit
  end if
end do
! Inspect TASK; an exit is not necessarily convergence.

local.name: LightConvex
local.description: Prototype linear-programming solvers in modern Fortran.

classifications.notes: The README explicitly restricts the current prototype to linear programs and marks a dense primal simplex implementation. Quadratic programming, sparse solvers and other unchecked roadmap items are not presented as implemented capabilities.

The public LINEAR_PROGRAM constructor assembles a dense tableau for maximizing C-transpose*X with nonnegative variables and supplied <=, >= or equality blocks; RHS vectors must be nonnegative within epsilon. SOLVE with PRIMALSIMPLEX dispatches auxiliary-function feasibility initialization and tableau pivots with Dantzig selection. It updates status on the PROBLEM object, then allocates primal X/slacks/objective only on an optimal status. The declared solution Y/T fields are not populated by this path. MAXITER bounds the phase-two loop, not a reviewed total phase-one evaluation budget. The inspected scope is the LP constructor/high-level dispatch and tableau iteration, not the advertised QP/KKT features or all phase-one edge cases. No feasibility/duality or numerical accuracy was verified by execution.

procedures.summary: Public generic returning DENSE_LP_TYPE. C(:) and matched optional matrix/RHS constraint pairs use project DP. Variables are nonnegative. Normalize negative RHS constraints before calling; construction assertions can terminate on invalid shapes or RHS values.

use lightconvex_constants, only: dp,ilp
use LightConvex, only: dense_lp_type,lp_solution,PrimalSimplex, &
     linear_program,solve,is_optimal
type(dense_lp_type) :: problem
type(lp_solution) :: solution
type(PrimalSimplex) :: alg
real(dp) :: a(2,2)
a=reshape([1.0_dp,0.0_dp,0.0_dp,1.0_dp],[2,2])
problem=linear_program([1.0_dp,1.0_dp],Aleq=a,bleq=[1.0_dp,2.0_dp])
alg=PrimalSimplex(maxiter=1000_ilp)
solution=solve(problem,alg)
if (.not. is_optimal(problem)) error stop "LP not optimal"
! Only now inspect solution%x/solution%s/objective_value; reference cost is 3.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. SOLVE mutates the tableau and the status belongs to PROBLEM. Do not use solution fields after nonoptimal return, or assume Y/T dual fields were populated. Requires stdlib, LightKrylov and the project dependencies; the source uses modern IMPLICIT NONE(EXTERNAL) declarations. The author tests are linked as context, not executed here.

procedures.summary: Public generic selecting the dense primal-simplex solve. PROBLEM is INOUT, ALG is a PrimalSimplex configuration, and the result is LP_SOLUTION. Call IS_OPTIMAL(PROBLEM) before reading primal fields.

HYBRD1 checks N/tolerance/workspace and configures HYBRD with dense forward-difference Jacobians, unit scaling, initial trust-region factor 100 and evaluation budget 200*(N+1). The inspected HYBRD driver dispatches FDJAC1, QR factorization and dogleg steps, with residual evaluations and progress tests. F2 records square nonlinear systems, not least-squares fitting or enumeration of every root. INFO=1 can indicate small relative steps, so independently inspect FVEC; it is not proof of a small residual or unique root. Negative callback IFLAG aborts. No finite-difference kernel, QR/dogleg arithmetic or numerical solve was fully verified.

procedures.summary: External double-precision square-system solver, also declared by module minpack. X(N) is input initial guess/output solution; FVEC(N) residual, WA length at least N*(3*N+13)/2. Default INTEGER dimensions/status. Check INFO and residuals. Callback FCN(N,X,FVEC,IFLAG) supplies values; no user Jacobian.
procedures.signature: CALL hybrd1(fcn, n, x, fvec, tol, info, wa, lwa)
procedures.usage:
use minpack, only: hybrd1
external :: fcn
integer, parameter :: n=2, lwa=n*(3*n+13)/2
integer :: info
double precision :: x(n), residual(n), work(lwa), tol
x=1.0d0
tol=sqrt(epsilon(1.0d0))
call hybrd1(fcn,n,x,residual,tol,info,work,lwa)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled calling fragment. Supply a matching FCN implementation; the linked author example shows its signature and a nine-variable problem. Link the full MINPACK dependencies and use matching double precision/default INTEGER. Inspect INFO and norm of residual before accepting a root; this fragment intentionally makes no root-accuracy assertion.

classifications.notes: LMDER1 configures LMDER for unconstrained nonlinear L2 least squares with supplied residual Jacobian, M>=N, relative cost/step tolerances and evaluation budget 100*(N+1). The inspected driver uses pivoted QR and Levenberg-Marquardt parameter/step dispatch. K1b1a2 records smooth unconstrained nonlinear least squares with user first derivatives, not arbitrary-objective optimization, bounds or rank-certified parameter identification. INFO=1..4 describe different normal stopping tests, not a zero-residual guarantee. The repository module callback interface declares IFLAG INTENT(IN) and both residual/Jacobian INTENT(OUT), conflicting with the classic preserve-the-unused-array/abort contract. The sketch uses the external routine and requires a correctly declared callback. No fit or Jacobian was checked and subordinate linear algebra is not audited.

procedures.summary: External double-precision Levenberg-Marquardt driver. M>=N>0; X(N), FVEC(M), FJAC(LDFJAC,N), LDFJAC>=M; IPVT(N); WA length >=5*N+M. Callback IFLAG=1 requests residuals, 2 Jacobian; preserve the other array and permit negative IFLAG termination. Use the external interface with that contract; the bundled module callback intents need correction.
procedures.signature: CALL lmder1(fcn, m, n, x, fvec, fjac, ldfjac, tol, info, ipvt, wa, lwa)

external :: lmder1, fcn
integer, parameter :: m=3, n=2, lwa=5*n+m
integer :: info, pivots(n)
double precision :: x(n), residual(m), jac(m,n), work(lwa), tol
x=1.0d0
tol=sqrt(epsilon(1.0d0))
call lmder1(fcn,m,n,x,residual,jac,m,tol,info,pivots,work,lwa)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled fragment; provide FCN(M,N,X,FVEC,FJAC,LDFJAC,IFLAG). Keep unused callback output storage defined; do not copy the module interface INTENT(OUT) declarations indiscriminately. Independently validate Jacobian and residual/cost; INFO alone is not parameter accuracy or full-rank certification. Link complete MINPACK support routines.

local.name: LMBM
local.description: Limited-memory bundle methods for large-scale unconstrained nonsmooth optimization.

classifications.notes: The lmbm.f interface documentation specifies unconstrained nonsmooth problems and initialization/workspace controls. It is not classified as a smooth-gradient solver or a constrained optimizer.

The public LMBMU entry validates dimension/memory controls, partitions caller workspace and dispatches the limited-memory bundle core. The inspected core calls linked FUNDER for objective/subgradient, maintains bundle data, chooses BFGS/SR1/skip update paths, distinguishes serious/null iteration work and checks stationarity/function-progress/evaluation/iteration/time limits. This is unconstrained multivariate nonsmooth minimization requiring a subgradient, not derivative-free search or a global optimality guarantee. FUNDER is linked rather than passed as an argument. IOUT(3) distinguishes successful stationarity, small-progress/budget exits and failures; not every positive code means a solved problem. Review covers entry/interface and core dispatch/stopping structure, not every bundle/line-search/matrix helper or numerical accuracy.

procedures.summary: External initializer/driver. N>0, NA>=2, MCU>=3, correction count MC, workspace length NW; X/F/RPAR/W are DOUBLE PRECISION, IPAR/IOUT integers, but TIME and RTIM(2) are default REAL. RPAR has eight controls, IPAR seven, IOUT three. Required NW is given in the linked source prologue. FUNDER(N,X,F,G,ITERM) must return both objective and subgradient.
procedures.signature: CALL LMBMU(N, NA, MCU, MC, NW, X, F, RPAR, IPAR, IOUT, TIME, RTIM, W)
procedures.usage:
! Initialize X, RPAR(8), IPAR(7), MC and the documented workspace.
! Declare default-REAL TIME, RTIM(2), not DOUBLE PRECISION.
! Link FUNDER and LMBM support routines; FUNDER sets ITERM on evaluation failure.
call lmbmu(n,na,mcu,mc,nw,x,f,rpar,ipar,iout,time,rtim,w)
! Inspect IOUT(3) and independently assess the returned point.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The calling fragment does not provide a problem or initialize all tuning controls. Respect NW >= 1+9*N+2*N*NA+3*NA+2*N*(MCU+1)+3*(MCU+2)*(MCU+1)/2+9*(MCU+1). IOUT(3)=1 denotes the method stationarity test; codes 2/3 and 4/5/6 are progress or budget/time exits, not an interchangeable success status. No test problem or convergence comparison was run.

classifications.notes: The README identifies a translation of the Weinert smoothing algorithm. Smoothing is not exact interpolation, and claimed speed improvement is not independently benchmarked.

CSPLINE forms second differences of equally spaced observations, factors a structured smoothing system using an untruncated or truncated recurrence, reconstructs the fitted values, evaluates a GCV-style score and fills intermediate/end samples. K5 records smoothing rather than exact interpolation through the supplied data. The user supplies LAM; returning SCORE does not mean the routine automatically minimizes GCV or chooses LAM. T enters through LAM*T**3, R selects subdivision/output layout and JJ controls recurrence truncation. There are no argument checks or status output. Small N and truncated recurrence sizes can cause invalid indexing; divisions/logarithms and score trace need valid nondegenerate inputs. The source review does not establish a general admissible parameter region or numerical stability.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine using REAL*8. Y(N) is input, X(R*N+R-1), XONY(N) and SCORE are outputs. Fitted original-node values occupy X(R:R*N:R); other entries are intermediate samples and end extensions. This is a regular-grid routine, not an arbitrary-abscissa spline API.
procedures.signature: CALL cspline(X, XONY, SCORE, Y, N, R, T, JJ, LAM)
procedures.usage:
use mcspline, only: cspline
integer, parameter :: n=12, r=2
real(kind(1d0)) :: y(n), x(r*n+r-1), fitted(n), score
integer :: j
y = [(real(j,kind(1d0)),j=1,n)]
call cspline(x,fitted,score,y,n,r,0.1d0,6,5.8d0)
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The sketch follows the author test sizes/controls and does not establish their accuracy or safety generally. REAL*8 is a compiler extension; confirm its kind matches the compiled module. Do not infer that LAM=0 is safe or that any positive N/R is accepted. Supply application-level validation and inspect finite outputs. No smoothing-parameter search was performed.

local.name: Linear System Solvers bridge
local.description: Fortran bridge to third-party linear-system solver libraries.

classifications.notes: The README documents makefiles and describes the project as a bridge. CMake support is an unchecked to-do item; no particular external solver, storage format or completed CMake path is inferred.

The public LIS_LINEAR_SOLVER_T bindings build a real sparse CSR operator/vectors, select LIS options and dispatch LIS_SOLVE for a previously initialized system, then copy vector values back. This mapping records the inspected real sparse-system adapter and backend dispatch, not an independent implementation or verification of every selectable LIS iterative method. CSR arrays are passed directly to LIS_MATRIX_SET_CSR with no index conversion; use the linked LIS convention and compatible integer/real ABI. Most backend IERR results, including LIS_SOLVE, are ignored rather than returned. RHS length is not explicitly asserted although XI/XO lengths are, and absent operator state ERROR STOPs. Each build initializes LIS and finalization destroys objects, so lifetime/reinitialization and MPI integration need separate validation.

procedures.summary: Public inherited/overridden type binding taking REAL(WP) XI/RHS/XO arrays, WP=SELECTED_REAL_KIND(15,307). Build the solver first using its public Build_lsys_solver_wth_arr or Build_lsys_solver_wth_mat binding. There is no returned convergence/status argument.
procedures.usage:
use mod_aux_precision, only: wp
use mod_lis_linear_solver, only: lis_linear_solver_t
type(lis_linear_solver_t) :: solver
! Initialize contiguous PTR/INDX/VAL using the linked LIS CSR convention.
! Provide NVAR and compatible REAL(WP) XI/RHS/XO vectors of length NVAR.
call solver%Build_lsys_solver_wth_arr(nvar,ptr,indx,val)
call solver%Keep_lsys_ops_and_solve(xi,rhs,xo)
! Independently compute the residual; returning XO does not certify LIS success.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Requires preprocessing lisf.h, LIS and the supporting project modules/libraries. The no-file build takes LIS defaults; public options fields are not established as an automatically applied configuration by this fragment. No particular Krylov/preconditioner is classified or tested. Backend error propagation, array shapes and object/runtime lifetime need attention before production reliance.

local.name: FTLIB
local.description: Fortran numerical library exposing rectangle, trapezoidal and Gaussian quadrature interfaces.

classifications.notes: The short README is supplemented by the quadrature module interface for sampled/function input and Gaussian rules. These interface declarations do not establish the correctness of every implementation or broader numerical method in the repository.

The inspected array overload accumulates 0.5*(x(i+1)-x(i))*(f(i)+f(i+1)), a composite trapezoidal integral of sampled data. H2a1b2 records nonautomatic grid-data quadrature, including nonuniform spacing, not a tolerance-driven callback integrator. Caller must provide ordered nodes and matching arrays; empty/singleton arrays produce zero. The parent declares a separate callback trapezoidal_rule_f but this submodule only supplies the array body. Plain FUNCTION headers in these submodules differ from the parent MODULE FUNCTION declarations and build compatibility was not checked. Mismatch handling delegates to an unreviewed print_error_message policy. No integral or build was executed.

procedures.summary: Public generic in ftlib_quadrature, scoped to array samples X(:), F(:) in DP=selected_real_kind(15,307), returning one DP scalar. It supplies no error estimate/status and does not validate node order. This is distinct from the declared callback overload, whose body was not found in this submodule.
procedures.usage:
use ftlib_kinds, only: dp
use ftlib_quadrature, only: trapezoidal_rule
real(dp) :: x(3), f(3), value
x=[0.0_dp,0.5_dp,1.0_dp]
f=x
value=trapezoidal_rule(x,f)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled fragment with expected integral 0.5. Parent/submodule procedure-definition consistency and the missing callback binding need build checking before presenting this as runnable library support. Use matching ordered arrays; no truncation estimate or tolerance test was performed.

classifications.notes: The inspected 1D Gaussian path obtains tabulated Gauss-Legendre nodes/weights for N=1..5, maps them affinely from [-1,1] to the first two endpoint entries, evaluates a procedure pointer and scales the weighted sum by half the interval length. H2a1a2 records nonautomatic finite-interval callback quadrature; no tolerance/error estimator is present. Unsupported N has no SELECT CASE default and leaves rule data undefined. The callback pointer must be associated, endpoints must have at least two entries, and its optional parameter-array convention must match. Plain submodule FUNCTION versus parent MODULE FUNCTION consistency needs build checking; multidimensional behavior is unreviewed. No quadrature result was executed.

procedures.summary: Public generic scoped to 1D endpoint vector X, type(function_type) F and default-INTEGER N=1..5. Callback is scalar function of DP X(:), optional DP ARGS(:); assign F%f and handle F%args consistently. Returns one DP scalar. The endpoints use X(1:2); this is not an array of integration nodes.
procedures.usage:
use ftlib_kinds, only: dp
use ftlib_function, only: function_type, function_procedure
use ftlib_quadrature, only: gaussian_quadrature
procedure(function_procedure) :: integrand
type(function_type) :: f
real(dp) :: value
f%f=>integrand
allocate(f%args(0))
value=gaussian_quadrature([0.0_dp,1.0_dp],f,3)
procedures.usage_notes: Uncompiled fragment. Supply the exact callback interface linked above, for example integrand(x,args)=x(1)**2 with unused optional args. Its expected integral 1/3 was not checked. Limit N to 1..5; no unsupported-order status is returned. Resolve/check submodule declaration consistency and all parent bindings before claiming build support. No multidimensional or other-rule accuracy was established.

classifications.notes: The brief README identifies a Fortran 90 signal-transform program and these two wavelet families. Normalization conventions, boundary treatment and numerical accuracy need source/example review; other wavelet families are not inferred.

The inspected program evaluates Morlet or Mexican-hat kernels at each integer scale and translation, multiplies by sampled signal and applies a trapezoidal weighted sum before writing coefficient magnitudes. This is a direct demonstrative continuous-wavelet-transform implementation, kept in the verified broad integral-transform class J rather than inventing a finer wavelet code. Quadrature omits time-step factors, translations use sample indices rather than input times, and the Morlet path uses default COMPLEX even though times are real(kind=8). No inverse transform, phase-preserving output, arbitrary-grid normalization or acceleration is established. Internal procedures belong to the program and are not reusable public module interfaces. File/allocation controls are not robustly validated; a malformed input can STOP the process.

procedures.summary: Standalone PROGRAM, not a linkable module API. Command argument 1 names a four-line parameter file; absent argument prompts for a file name. The program reads an input basename plus .dat and writes a prefixed scalogram file. Its contained wavelet/quadrature functions are internal helpers.
procedures.usage:
gfortran cwt.f90 -o cwt
./cwt cwt.par
procedures.usage_notes: Invocation sketch only; no compilation or execution was performed. Supply the four parameter records: input basename, output prefix, number of scales, wavelet selector (0 Morlet / 1 Mexican hat). Input .dat starts with sample count followed by time/value rows. The supplied cwt.par references CO1.dat. Output coefficients are magnitudes only. Treat time as unit-spaced sample coordinates and validate normalization independently; internal helpers do not use actual time differences in quadrature.

local.name: Fortran Metrics
local.description: Forecast-error measures including bias, absolute errors and RMSE.

classifications.notes: The README lists scalar/vector error metrics and automatic missing-data skipping. These routines assess predictions; they do not themselves produce forecasts. Missing-value and zero-denominator behavior need more detailed review.

The vector calc binding forms prediction-minus-observation errors after removing pairs matching the -999 sentinel, then returns N, mean bias, mean absolute error, root mean squared error and a percentage summary. L1 records data/error summarization; these are not confidence intervals or distribution tests. The implemented vector MAPE is SUM(ABS(error)/observation*100)/N, with a signed observation denominator: negative observations can give negative contributions and zero observations divide by zero. Scalar APE instead takes ABS of the percentage error. Arrays must conform, default REAL precision is used, and sentinel matching is not IEEE NaN handling. No outputs were checked by execution.

procedures.summary: Public generic type binding, shown for its rank-one vector overload. Predictions yhat and observations y are conformable default-REAL vectors; results are public components of metrics_ty. The scalar overload fills different components. Missing pairs are excluded using NA=-999; all missing sets N=iNA and vector summaries to NA.
procedures.usage:
use metrics_mo, only: metrics_ty
type(metrics_ty) :: metrics
call metrics%calc([2.0, 4.0], [1.0, 3.0])
print *, metrics%N, metrics%MBE, metrics%MAE, metrics%RMSE
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Use equal-length finite arrays and positive nonzero observations if using percentage summaries. Legitimate values near the NA sentinel are treated as missing. Vector MAPE uses signed y, not ABS(y). Read components for the active overload only; the object does not reset every component on every call. Allocatable assignment/reallocation is used internally.

local.name: Differential Evolution F95
local.description: Basic differential-evolution optimizer with a Griewank-function example.

classifications.notes: The README identifies DE/rand/1/bin with dithering and reports early grid locking for the example. Suggested larger populations or ad hoc perturbations are upstream workarounds, not independently established reliability or global convergence.

DIFF_EVOL implements a stochastic differential-evolution search using mutation, binomial-style crossover, greedy selection and optional population perturbation. It calls the module-specific Griewank OBJ_FTN directly rather than accepting an objective callback. Lower/upper bounds initialize/reinitialize the population but do not constrain later mutation trials. Source findings: donor rejection uses AND rather than OR, so indices need not be distinct/exclude the target; the forced crossover coordinate can be NOP+1; BH_BEST is assigned only after improvement over the initial minimum and can remain undefined. G2i records the intended global-search method, not a guarantee of a global solution, correct bounded DE, or fitness for production use. The fixed generation/progress logic prints each generation and exposes no status or evaluation count.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine using DE_MOD::DP=SELECTED_REAL_KIND(12,100). NOP/NP/T/PD are integer, LB/UB/BH_BEST vectors, F_LO/F_HI/CR real controls and F_BEST scalar output. The objective must be changed in the module to use a different problem; no callback argument exists.
procedures.signature: CALL Diff_Evol(NOP, NP, LB, UB, T, F_LO, F_HI, CR, PD, BH_BEST, F_BEST)
procedures.usage:
use DE_mod, only: dp,Diff_Evol
real(dp) :: lower(2),upper(2),best(2),cost
lower=-5.0_dp; upper=5.0_dp
call Diff_Evol(2,20,lower,upper,100,0.5_dp,0.9_dp,0.8_dp,0,best,cost)
! This calls the built-in Griewank objective.
! BEST may be undefined if no improvement occurred; repair before relying on it.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Interface illustration only, not a recommended checked optimizer. Use valid positive dimensions/population and probability controls, but those do not fix the donor/crossover/output/bounds findings. Seed RANDOM_NUMBER externally for reproducibility. No trial population, returned optimum or global-search performance was checked.

local.name: Minimize routines
local.description: Steepest descent, conjugate-gradient and BFGS optimization with line searches.

classifications.notes: The README lists quadratic-interpolation and golden-section line minimization and directs users to test_minimize.F90. Interface and convergence assumptions need further review; a test executable being supplied is not a test result here.

The inspected STEEPEST_DESCENT entry uses a user objective and array-valued gradient, normalizes the descent direction, dispatches quadratic line interpolation with golden-section fallback, and tests mean squared gradient and relative cost change. Only this local smooth supplied-gradient method is mapped here, not the unreviewed CG/BFGS entries in the same file. Source findings: normalization precedes the zero-gradient test, relative cost change divides by the previous cost, and a SAVE allocatable gradient is allocated only once without resizing. The README documents a Makefile and FFTW3 dependency; the calculus module supplies derivative/integral interfaces and implementation comments. Coverage is kept to the reviewed module rather than inferred from every source filename; stopping tolerances are not independently certified error bounds.

The public DERIVATIVE generic selects private 1D/2D functions. The inspected 1D path computes centered differences with initial width one, halves the width and stops after at least five iterations when ABS(DNEW/DOLD-1)<ACC. It has a fixed 100-iteration maximum and STOPs on exhaustion. Arithmetic and callback use default REAL, not the separate precision module. Zero previous derivative estimates lead to division by zero, and a relative successive-estimate test is not a rigorous derivative error bound. The finite-difference path is numerical differentiation, not automatic differentiation or a review of the library integration/domain modules.

procedures.summary: Public module generic; inspected scalar 1D binding returns default REAL and takes a default-REAL callback F(X), point X and accuracy control ACC. The callback input has INTENT(IN). Import DERIVATIVE, not the private DERIVATIVE_1D specific.

local.name: PROPACK
local.description: Lanczos bidiagonalization for singular values and vectors of large sparse or structured matrices.

classifications.notes: The distribution README documents partial reorthogonalization and restarted/nonrestarted variants. Their memory/convergence tradeoffs and dated platform configurations are recorded as documentation, not verified current compiler or performance results.

The nonrestarted real DLANSVD driver dispatches Lanczos bidiagonalization with partial reorthogonalization, solves the projected bidiagonal SVD, refines Ritz error estimates and extends the Krylov space until requested singular triplets converge or the space is exhausted. APROD must supply both A*x and A-transpose*x. Singular-vector reconstruction is dispatched only on the driver completion conditions. K is overwritten with the number obtained, and INFO distinguishes ordinary completion, smaller invariant subspace and failed convergence. Caller workspace, callback correctness and options are essential; the few scalar guards are not a complete input validator. LAPINFO from the bidiagonal solver is not propagated as a checked caller status in the inspected path. No callback, singular triplet or numerical error bound was verified by execution; restarted/complex variants remain unreviewed.

procedures.summary: External DOUBLE PRECISION callback-based truncated SVD driver. U(LDU,KMAX+1), V(LDV,KMAX), SIGMA/BND and documented WORK/IWORK storage are required even when only values are wanted. Pass K as a variable: it is changed on return. JOBU/JOBV select singular-vector reconstruction; TOLIN controls the driver convergence threshold.
procedures.signature:
CALL DLANSVD(JOBU, JOBV, M, N, K, KMAX, APROD, U, LDU, SIGMA, BND, &
     V, LDV, TOLIN, WORK, LWORK, IWORK, LIWORK, DOPTION, IOPTION, INFO, DPARM, IPARM)
procedures.usage:
! Allocate U/V, SIGMA/BND and documented mode-dependent workspaces.
! Implement APROD(TRANSA,M,N,X,Y,DPARM,IPARM) for N and T operations.
u(:,1)=0.0d0  ! request generated starting vector
ioption=[0,1]
doption=[sqrt(epsilon(1.0d0)),epsilon(1.0d0)**0.75d0,0.0d0]
call dlansvd("Y","Y",m,n,k,kmax,aprod,u,ldu,sigma,bnd,v,ldv, &
     tol,work,lwork,iwork,liwork,doption,ioption,info,dparm,iparm)
! Inspect INFO and returned K before using singular triplets.

Use the exact WORK/IWORK lower bounds linked in the declarations; no compact substitute workspace formula is implied. Initialize the statistics COMMON state as the author example does. The .F source needs preprocessing, stat.h and supporting PROPACK/BLAS/LAPACK routines. Independently check A*v-sigma*u, A^T*u-sigma*v and orthogonality; the reported bounds are not independently certified.

local.name: qrupdate-ng
local.description: Fast QR, Cholesky and LU factorization updates and downdates.

classifications.notes: The README lists rank-one updates and row/column insertion/deletion/shift operations, with different restrictions by factorization. It explicitly distinguishes pivoted and unpivoted LU stability; not every update operation applies to every stored factorization.

DQR1UP updates an existing real QR factorization after A -> A+u*v-transpose. It forms Q-transpose*u, applies Givens rotations to factors, updates the leading row and retriangularizes; the economy branch additionally handles the component orthogonal to the basis and dispatches a Cholesky update. This is decomposition updating, not a fresh QR factorizer or a linear solver. Inputs must already form a valid full/economy factorization. Q/R and V are overwritten, U can be destroyed in economy form, and WORK needs 2*K elements. Invalid scalar dimensions go through QRUPDATE_XERROR; no status dummy is returned. Review covers this driver/rotation dispatch, not every helper, downdate or complex variant.

procedures.summary: External real64 subroutine. Q is M-by-K, R K-by-N, with K=M (full) or K=N<M (economy). LDQ>=M and LDR>=K; U(M), V(N), W(2*K). Match the library default-integer/BLAS ABI. Configure error handling if process termination by the default handler is unsuitable.
procedures.signature: CALL dqr1up(M, N, K, Q, LDQ, R, LDR, U, V, W)
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
real(real64) :: q(2,2),r(2,2),u(2),v(2),work(4)
q=reshape([1.0_real64,0.0_real64,0.0_real64,1.0_real64],[2,2])
r=reshape([2.0_real64,0.0_real64,0.0_real64,3.0_real64],[2,2])
u=[1.0_real64,0.5_real64]; v=[0.25_real64,1.0_real64]
call dqr1up(2,2,2,q,2,r,2,u,v,work)

The PROGRAM contains its fitting helpers; they are not externally callable public library routines. In the independent-coefficient path, the code builds sums of weighted powers of shifted abscissae, factors and inverts the symmetric normal matrix via DSYTRF/DSYTRI, multiplies by the weighted data vector, and accumulates weighted squared residuals. No upstream code or author example was compiled or run.

classifications.notes: The README documents a scalar loss callback, parameter bounds and topology controls; additional optimizers are future plans. It refers to opti in installation examples, while this reviewed repository identity remains Konrad1991/pso.

The public OPTIMIZER initializes random particles, evaluates a scalar callback, updates velocity from inertial/personal/social terms and clamps coordinates to bounds. It retains personal/global best costs and returns a parameter vector after a generation budget or desired-cost threshold. The inspected scope is the star topology (TOPO=1); adaptive-neighborhood logic is not independently reviewed. Source findings: the star social index is selected initially and not refreshed in the general generation loop, and the returned global-best parameters are copied from the particle current position rather than its saved personal-best position. They can therefore disagree with the stored best error. There is no returned objective/status; desired_error is an objective threshold rather than parameter accuracy. This is heuristic global search, not a global-optimum guarantee or a validated convergence result.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine in PSOMOD. REAL(8) LB/UB/RESULT have N_PARAMS entries; FCT(INP,PROBLEM_SIZE) returns REAL(8) for a vector input with INTENT(IN). classifications.notes: The README describes suitability for noisy or discontinuous objectives and attributes the algorithm to Tom Rowan. Such suitability is method guidance, not a guarantee for every noise model or discontinuity.

SUBPLX sorts step scales, partitions coordinates into subspaces and calls SIMPLX for derivative-free simplex minimization, repeating until its relative coordinate/step test is satisfied or a limit is returned. The nonsmooth unconstrained class records this local search, not global optimization. Unlike older comments, this fork has no MODE argument and always initializes default options through SUBOPT. TRDF performs a constrained derivative-free objective trust-region iteration: it dispatches a feasibility solve, builds a quadratic interpolation model, solves a constrained model subproblem, evaluates the true objective and updates radius/model geometry. Constraints can mix equalities/inequalities and bound constraints; CCODED selects whether linked constraint Jacobian/Hessian routines are supplied. This review covers outer iteration/linked-problem dispatch, not all model algebra or ALGENCAN kernels. The interface requires linked CALOBJF/CALCON and optional derivative routines via functions.f, not procedure arguments. COMMON state and compile-time dimensions in tr_params.par limit reentrancy/size. An alternate model-build path calls CALFUN with three arguments although its wrapper takes four; this mismatch needs repair/checked validation. The routine returns F/FEAS/FCNT but no termination flag, and early failure can reach output code before a valid final model point exists. No feasibility or optimizer result was run.

procedures.summary: External DOUBLE PRECISION constrained objective-minimization routine. X/XL/XU length N, EQUATN/LINEAR length M, CCODED(2), explicit model/evaluation/radius controls and scalar F/FEAS/FCNT outputs. Supply compatible linked objective/constraint evaluators and subproblem solver. EQUATN marks equality; inequalities use CALCON<=0.
procedures.signature:
CALL TRDF(N, NPT, X, XL, XU, M, EQUATN, LINEAR, CCODED, &
     MAXFCNT, RBEG, REND, XEPS, F, FEAS, FCNT)
procedures.usage:
! Initialize X, bounds, constraint flags and model/budget controls.
! Link CALOBJF/CALCON (and coded constraint derivatives), functions.f and SOLVER.
call trdf(n,npt,x,xl,xu,m,equatn,linear,ccoded,maxfcnt, &
     rbeg,rend,xeps,f,feas,fcnt)
! Independently reevaluate objective and constraint violations at returned X.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This is not a self-contained callback driver. The source mismatch/early-failure behavior should be repaired before relying on checked builds. Fixed-form preprocessing of tr_params.par and the external constrained solver/dependencies are required. EASYTRDF defaults to a 100000 evaluation budget; explicit controls are preferable for bounded experiments. No derivative-free constraint guarantee is inferred when CCODED requests derivatives.

local.name: ucminf
local.description: R/Fortran unconstrained quasi-Newton minimization with BFGS updating.

classifications.notes: The README documents soft line search with trust-region-style monitoring and an optim-like interface. The example and convergence behavior were not reproduced; this is not classified as constrained optimization.

The UCMINF core forms an inverse-Hessian search direction, limits its length, performs a soft line search and updates a packed inverse Hessian by BFGS when a curvature test permits it. This mapping is scoped to supplied first derivatives: the R frontend sets GRAD=0 when GR is provided; FDF dispatches objective/gradient through linked C routines evaluating an R environment. The fork removed the FDF callback argument from the Fortran entry. RHO is an opaque runtime handle, not an ordinary user integer work array. This is local smooth unconstrained optimization, not a standalone Fortran callback solver or a certified trust-region method.

local.name: vc-SQNM
local.description: Stabilized quasi-Newton optimization including variable-cell-shape minimization.

classifications.notes: The README identifies Fortran, C++ and Python implementations and an extension that also optimizes lattice vectors. Reliability and speed claims remain upstream claims; detailed algorithm equivalence and physical model coverage need later review.

The reusable Fortran SQNM_OPTIMIZER takes externally computed objective values/gradients, retains displacement/gradient histories, diagonalizes history and Hessian subspaces and returns a stabilized quasi-Newton displacement. The caller applies X<-X+STEP and reevaluates; SQNM_STEP does not call a user objective or overwrite X. Initialization configures history length, step scale/floor and subspace threshold; CLOSE_SQNM releases buffers. An internal max-gradient cutoff of 1e-11 returns a zero step, but application convergence/budgets are otherwise caller responsibilities. Degenerate history/eigenvalue divisions need valid inputs; LAPACK failures STOP, with no returned status. Only this fixed-coordinate unconstrained smooth supplied-gradient optimizer is mapped, not variable-cell/atomistic wrappers or a rigorous lower-bound guarantee.

procedures.summary: Public type-bound method on SQNM_OPTIMIZER in module SQNM. X/gradient/step use REAL(C_DOUBLE); X is INTENT(IN). Initialize with INTEGER(C_INT) dimensions/history and compatible real controls first, then close explicitly. No success/error output is provided.
procedures.usage:
use iso_c_binding, only: c_int,c_double
use sqnm, only: sqnm_optimizer
type(sqnm_optimizer) :: opt
real(c_double) :: x(2),gradient(2),step(2),value
integer :: iteration
x=[2.0_c_double,-1.0_c_double]
call opt%initialize_sqnm(2_c_int,5_c_int,0.1_c_double, &
     0.001_c_double,1.0e-4_c_double)
do iteration=1,100
  value=sum(x*x); gradient=2.0_c_double*x
  if (maxval(abs(gradient)) < 1.0e-8_c_double) exit
  call opt%sqnm_step(x,value,gradient,step)
  x=x+step
end do
call opt%close_sqnm()
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The quadratic loop illustrates ownership of evaluation/update/stopping; it is not a checked driver. Reevaluate the final point if the loop budget is exhausted. Do not change the returned displacement independently without understanding the history consistency contract. Reinitializing an allocated object requires cleanup; zero/singular history and all helper kernels were not validated.

The inspected public BINOMIALCOEF returns individual binomial coefficients as REAL64, using a stored Pascal table through n=20 and BINOMIALCOEFSARRAY Pascal recurrence above that. The array routine reconstructs each row from the previous row with endpoint ones. This is the GAMS integer-valued combinatorial-function scope, although the representation is floating point rather than exact arbitrary-size integers. For n>=0, out-of-range j returns zero. Negative n is not a supported validated input and large coefficients lose exactness or overflow; the routines return no status. Other utility modules and the separate table-generating API are not promoted by this source review.

procedures.summary: Public PURE module function. Default-integer N/J arguments; REAL64 result. Requires nonnegative N. Although the mathematical value is integral, do not interpret all returned floating-point values as exact integers.
procedures.usage:
use iso_fortran_env, only: real64
use binomial_coefficients, only: binomialCoef
real(real64) :: value
value = binomialCoef(10,3)
! Compare with the exact reference 120.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. This small reference lies in the stored-table branch. The recurrence for larger N has floating-point range/exactness limits and workspace proportional to N. Neither large-order behavior nor all utility routines were tested.

procedures.summary: Public PURE subroutine returning the full nth Pascal row in REAL64 BINCOEFS(0:N), declared INTENT(INOUT) but initialized internally. Default integer N must be nonnegative.

classifications.notes: The README identifies scalar/multivariate differentiation and a modified DNAD basis. Its zero-truncation-error statement for hyper-dual methods is not interpreted as absence of floating-point or implementation error.

The inspected FDM path forms central first differences with step 1e-6, diagonal second differences with step 1e-3, and mixed Hessian entries from simultaneous positive/negative perturbations after subtracting diagonal contributions. LIBRARY_REAL8::DIFF selects this path when GLOBAL::GRAD_PAR=1 and initializes gradient/Hessian outputs. The objective is not a passed callback: OBJ_FUNC dispatches fixed selectors 1 (x cubed), 2 (sine plus cosine with degree-to-radian conversion), or 3 (von Mises stress with additional GLOBAL dimension setup). A new objective requires adapting the included source consistently across the typed modules. H1 is the differentiation leaf; the review establishes finite-difference implementation structure, not derivative accuracy. The supplied main selects a different hyper-dual path, which is not audited here, and complex/hyper-dual algorithm correctness is not inferred from the README. Unsupported method selection leaves zero outputs and unsupported objective selection leaves ANS unassigned. No error/status or user step-size parameter is exposed. No driver was compiled or run.

CSPLREP constructs piecewise-cubic coefficients by solving a tridiagonal system for second derivatives with user-supplied endpoint curvatures; CSPLEV selects an interval and evaluates its local polynomial. Zero endpoint curvatures give a natural cubic spline. Require at least four matching sorted, well-separated data nodes. Source findings: fewer nodes return uninitialized coefficients, CSPLREP uses ALLOCATED(CSP%X).AND.SIZE(CSP%X) without guaranteed short-circuit evaluation, and the interval lookup can return 0 or N for outside/upper-end queries although coefficients have N-1 columns. Those queries are not safe extrapolation. The mapping covers fitting and scalar value evaluation, not derivative/integral/root helpers or a full dependency audit.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine using basic::DP=REAL64. X/Y are same-length vectors; S1/SN are endpoint second derivatives, not first derivatives. CSP is a CubicSpline output containing knots and local coefficients. There is no status dummy.
procedures.signature: CALL csplrep(X, Y, S1, SN, CSP)
procedures.usage:
use basic, only: dp
use csplines, only: CubicSpline,csplrep,csplev
type(CubicSpline) :: csp
real(dp) :: x(4), y(4), value
x=[0.0_dp,1.0_dp,2.0_dp,3.0_dp]; y=2.0_dp*x+1.0_dp
call csplrep(x,y,0.0_dp,0.0_dp,csp)
value=csplev(1.5_dp,csp)
! Linear data have analytic query value 4.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. The allocation-condition portability finding should be addressed before relying on checked builds. Use N>=4, strict increasing spacing above the library Small threshold and strictly interior queries. The constructor/other operations are not all verified. The pinned author example is context, not an executed catalog driver.

procedures.summary: Public generic; inspected scalar binding evaluates an existing CubicSpline. XC and result are REAL64; CSP is input. It directly uses the search result as a coefficient-column index without checking bounds.
procedures.usage:

value = csplev(xc,csp)

local.name: Pade Approximants
local.description: Fortran and Python analytic continuation using Pade rational approximations.

classifications.notes: The README distinguishes the Fortran Beach matrix-formulation path from extra Python algorithms and discusses double/quadruple inversion. Analytic continuation is sensitive to data and precision; the documented tests are not independent validation here.

The public ACPADE path (SOLVER=0) forms a Beach rational-approximation matrix with N=2*r coefficients, solves it in a least-squares sense and evaluates numerator degree r-1 over a monic degree-r denominator. This is rational/Padé approximation from sampled complex values, not a verified recovery of analytic continuation or guaranteed pole accuracy. The inspected scope uses NPRECISION=64 and MTR=0, dispatching standard ZGELS through double conversion; quad and SVD branches are not numerically audited. SOLVER=1 (Thiele) is explicitly unimplemented and STOPs. Even positive N, matched shapes, enough samples and a nonzero denominator are caller requirements. The low-level entry avoids reading pade.par but writes diagnostics to unit 90; the module also needs a generated gitversion include. Backend positive INFO can produce a log message and still return coefficients without a caller status.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine (no PRIVATE default). Z/F/ZOUT and coefficient X use COMPLEX(KIND=16), while FOUT is COMPLEX(KIND=8). Supply even N, X(N), FOUT(SIZE(ZOUT)), SIZE(F)=SIZE(Z) and at least N samples for the illustrated overdetermined solve. Controls remain default integer inputs without INTENT declarations.

The public BRENTZERO generic selects single/double bindings. The reviewed double binding tests endpoint roots/signs, maintains a bracket, attempts secant or inverse-quadratic interpolation and falls back to bisection when acceptance conditions fail. It returns an interval-scale convergence test or exact computed zero, evaluation count and explicit error code. The routine is for one continuous scalar equation with a sign-changing bracket, not guaranteed root enumeration, polynomial complex roots or discontinuous functions. The initial FA*FB sign test can overflow/underflow, and finite values/positive tolerances/iteration limits are not validated. No accuracy or pathological-bracket behavior was checked by execution.

procedures.summary: Public module generic; reviewed double binding uses SELECTED_REAL_KIND(10,50). Callback F(X) has a scalar real input with INTENT(IN) and scalar real result. ERRCode=0 normal, 1 iteration budget, 2 endpoints have the same sign; NEVAL counts endpoint and iteration evaluations.
procedures.signature: CALL BrentZero(AX, BX, F, TOL, MAXITER, NEVAL, ERRCODE, XZERO, FZERO)
procedures.usage:
use ForsytheMalcolmMoler, only: BrentZero
integer, parameter :: dp=selected_real_kind(10,50)
real(dp) :: root, residual

local.name: NNLS Fortran 2018
local.description: Nonnegative least-squares solver using BLAS and LAPACK.

classifications.notes: The README gives a solve interface and a randomized test harness with iteration/residual reporting. Multiple solutions may exist; small residuals do not prove recovery of a unique generated vector, and the tests were not run here.

The README gives a solve interface and a randomized test harness with iteration/residual reporting. Multiple solutions may exist; small residuals do not prove recovery of a unique generated vector, and the tests were not run here.

The inspected solve routine forms A-transpose A and A-transpose b, adds variables to a passive set according to the positive projected residual, solves passive normal equations through update_s/DSYSV, and moves toward feasible nonnegative coefficients before updating the residual. This supports constrained L2 least squares D9b1, specifically nonnegative coefficients, not general equality/inequality constraints or a rank-revealing QR method. The code overwrites X from zero and returns ||A X-b||. Material discrepancies: implementation sets MODE=1 and leaves it there on normal completion despite comments/README saying zero; -1 reports iteration exhaustion and returns infinite X/residual. The iteration counter advances only in the inner feasibility loop, so MAXITER is not a strict cap on all outer iterations or linear solves. update_s ignores INFO from both DSYSV workspace query and solve, so rank-deficient/singular normal equations have no safe reported fallback. Normal equations can amplify conditioning issues. No KKT, residual, rank-deficient case or execution was checked.

procedures.summary: Public module subroutine, also BIND(C,name="solve"). Fortran callers use module nnls. A(m,n), b(m), x(n), tolerance/residual use C_DOUBLE; dimension/mode/MAXITER scalars use C_INT. The binding lacks VALUE, so C scalar arguments are pointers. There are no INTENT declarations; pass variables rather than relying on input-only dummy semantics. A/b are not assigned in the inspected body; x is overwritten. Actual normal MODE is 1, not the documented 0.
procedures.signature: CALL solve(A, b, x, m, n, mode, res, maxiter, tol)

use iso_c_binding, only: c_double, c_int
use nnls, only: solve
integer(c_int) :: m, n, mode, maxiter
real(c_double) :: a(3,2), b(3), x(2), res, tol
m=3_c_int
n=2_c_int
maxiter=100_c_int
tol=1.0e-10_c_double
a(:,1)=[1.0_c_double,0.0_c_double,0.0_c_double]
a(:,2)=[0.0_c_double,1.0_c_double,0.0_c_double]
b=[-1.0_c_double,2.0_c_double,1.0_c_double]
call solve(a,b,x,m,n,mode,res,maxiter,tol)
if (mode /= 1_c_int) error stop "NNLS did not finish normally"

local.name: sampleSTAT

classifications.notes: The README documents means, sample standard deviations, extrema and confidence-level controls. Its IEEE-based portability and probability interpretations are not universal guarantees: distributional assumptions, rounding and compiler behavior require independent checking.

SampleStatistics::ArithMean calls Sums on X(1:N) and divides the sum by N. This supports location summaries of univariate raw data (L1a1a), not a statistical hypothesis-test mapping. REAL(DP) is selected in SysConst with SELECTED_REAL_KIND(15,307). N must be positive and no larger than SIZE(X); no input validation or status output is present. Summation is direct, not a compensated/streaming estimator. No numerical result or CLI workflow was run.

procedures.summary: REAL(DP) arithmetic-mean function over the first N entries of an assumed-shape vector. Import the module interface and SysConst kind; provide 1 <= N <= SIZE(X).
procedures.usage:
use SysConst, only: DP
use SampleStatistics, only: ArithMean
real(DP) :: x(3), mean
x = [1.0_DP, 2.0_DP, 3.0_DP]
mean = ArithMean(x, size(x))
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Compile SysConst before SampleStatistics; sysconst_mdl.F90 contains preprocessor directives. No empty-input, NaN or overflow protection is supplied by the reviewed routine.

classifications.notes: Variance computes (SUM(X**2)-SUM(X)**2/N)/(N-1) over X(1:N); StdDev returns its square root. L1a1b records dispersion of univariate raw data, specifically sample variance with N-1 denominator. Require 2 <= N <= SIZE(X). The subtractive raw-moment formula can lose precision for small spread around large offsets and can yield a negative computed variance; there is no status or clamp. This review does not cover the Student-factor/confidence routines or verify distributional assumptions by execution.

procedures.summary: REAL(DP) sample-variance function. N is a separate default integer selecting X(1:N). The denominator is N-1; this is not population variance.
procedures.usage:
use SysConst, only: DP
use SampleStatistics, only: Variance, StdDev
real(DP) :: x(3), v, sd
x = [1.0_DP, 2.0_DP, 3.0_DP]
v = Variance(x, size(x))
sd = StdDev(x, size(x))
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Require at least two finite samples. These raw-moment routines have no error status or cancellation protection. Source mapping is not a recommendation over numerically stable online/two-pass estimators.

The reviewed driver starts at the unconstrained quadratic minimizer, selects violated constraints, computes primal/dual steps, adds constraints with Givens rotations and removes constraints when a dual step requires it. G2e1 records positive-definite-Hessian quadratic programming; no indefinite or merely semidefinite extension is inferred. The objective is 0.5*x-transpose*P*x - x-transpose*q, with A*x=b and C*x>=d; sign and row orientation matter. The constructor checks dimensions but does not propagate TRTRI INFO, and its Cholesky call has no returned err argument. The unconstrained wrapper branch sets X and success but never assigns result%obj; the sketch therefore uses a constrained case. The boolean success loses detailed driver failure information, so validate returned feasibility/stationarity independently. Compact storage, least-squares/LASSO variants and external numerical kernels are not audited. No QP or author tests were executed. The linked inequality test transposes C despite the constructor row-storage interface; that example orientation needs checking and is not copied into the sketch.

procedures.summary: Public generic constructor for the dense standard problem. P(n,n) must be symmetric positive definite, q(n) gives the SUBTRACTED linear term. Optional A/b and C/d must occur in pairs, with one constraint per ROW. All arrays use dp=selected_real_kind(15,307). The constructor stores a factorization rather than the original P; reconstruct the object when changing P and preserve originals for residual/KKT checks.
procedures.signature: problem = qp_problem(P, q, A=A, b=b, C=C, d=d)

procedures.summary: Public generic, scoped to the standard qp_problem overload. Input problem is INTENT(IN); private working copies are modified. Returns OptimizeResult with x, multipliers y (equalities followed by inequalities), obj and success for a constrained solve. Check success before using outputs. The unconstrained return path leaves obj unset.

use QuadProg, only: dp, qp_problem, OptimizeResult, solve
type(qp_problem) :: problem
type(OptimizeResult) :: result
real(dp) :: p(2,2), q(2), c(2,2), d(2)
p=0.0_dp
p(1,1)=1.0_dp
p(2,2)=1.0_dp
q=[-1.0_dp,2.0_dp]
c=p
d=0.0_dp
problem=qp_problem(p,q,C=c,d=d)
result=solve(problem)
if (.not.result%success) error stop "QP did not finish successfully"

LININTERPOL searches for neighboring abscissae and evaluates an affine weighted pair, using a saved interval index for subsequent calls. The implemented interpolation is univariate piecewise linear. Despite header prose promising zero outside the table, those returns/assignments are commented out; search conditions may evaluate negative/out-of-range elements and the final formula extrapolates after clamping. The nold<1 check does not reject a one-point table. Even an in-range query on a two-point table can first read beyond the upper end because the saved-index clamp sets nold-1 then accesses ilastnum+1. Resetting ILASTVAL sets ILASTNUM=-1; a subsequent upward search can begin at -2 and read a negative index even for an in-range query. More table points do not repair this. The sketch records the interface only; the search requires repair and checked testing before use. This review does not establish flux conservation or review the spectral-resampling dispatcher.

procedures.summary: External subroutine using numeric RP=8 and IB=4 kinds from ModDataType. Table/query/output vectors use dummy lower bound zero; NOLD_VEC/NXYVALUE are explicit lengths. ILASTVAL is input/output (negative resets saved search state), ISKEEPON is output and VERBOSITY optional. An explicit interface is required.

query=[0.5_rp]; last=-999_ib

The public CEL function evaluates Bulirsch complete elliptic integral cel(kc,p,a,b) using a duplication iteration, transforming the p<=0 branch before iteration. The integral definition is explicitly given in source. This mapping covers the reusable special-function routine, not the domain-specific magnetic-field APIs or a claim of all elliptic-integral forms. Source finding: the kc=0 branch tests local B before assigning B_IN, so that branch reads undefined state; the declaration already requires nonzero kc. The loop has no explicit iteration limit/status output. Positive p and nonzero kc avoid the inspected singular-branch issue; the negative-p branch is not presented as an ordinary nonsingular integral.

procedures.summary: Public module function returning REAL64 via wp=>mod_kinds::dp. Arguments KC_IN, P_IN, A_IN, B_IN are real(wp) scalars; no status or error bound is returned. The complementary modulus KC is not the usual elliptic parameter m.
procedures.usage:
use mod_kinds, only: dp
use mod_cel, only: cel
real(dp) :: value
value = cel(1.0_dp,1.0_dp,1.0_dp,1.0_dp)
! For these inputs the defining integral is pi/2.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only; not compiled or run for this catalog. Keep KC nonzero and use positive P for the ordinary nonsingular integral illustrated here. The implementation moves whole columns for 2-D input; it is not independent sorting of every row. No stability guarantee, descending-history check or author example was executed.

procedures.summary: Public generic for in-place real vector sorting or sorting matrix columns by a reference row. history and reverse are optional; matrix aref selects the reference row. Specific msort implementation routines are private. Ascending examples are shown because the inspected descending wrappers reverse data without reversing history.
procedures.signature:
CALL sort(arr, history, reverse)
CALL sort(matrix, history, aref, reverse)
procedures.usage:
use merge_sort_mod, only: sort
! arr is an initialized array of a supported element kind.
call sort(arr)
! For labels: initialize history to [1,2,...,size(arr)] first.
! Then call sort(arr, history) for ascending order.
procedures.usage_notes: Calling sketch only. history and reverse may be omitted. For a matrix, use a valid reference-row index and one history label per column. Do not rely on descending history: the documented source-review finding remains unresolved. No sort result or edge case was checked by execution.

classifications.notes: The real(sp), real(dp) and real(qp) generic bindings overwrite a vector or permute complete matrix columns using one selected real reference row. The inspected double-precision wrappers and shared merge bodies support active internal real sorting (N6a2b). The optional history is moved during ascending merges; reverse=.true. reverses only the data in the inspected wrappers, so descending history correspondence is not verified and appears inconsistent. Real128 support, NaNs, signed-zero ordering, stability after reversal and extreme sizes were not checked. No passive-rank, character or complex-key mapping is inferred.

procedures.summary: Public generic for gathering companion values or matrix columns using reference_history. The data are overwritten; reference_history is an input integer index vector. The specific rearrange_* implementations are private. Caller-supplied indices must be valid for the input array.

use merge_sort_mod, only: rearrange
! Initialize companion data and a valid output-to-input index vector.
call rearrange(arr, reference_history)

Obtain history from a compatible ascending sort or construct a valid permutation yourself; the catalog does not claim this routine validates indices. classifications.notes: The public rearrange generic applies reference_history as a gather permutation. The included 1-D body copies arr(reference_history(i)); the 2-D body copies complete arr(:,reference_history(i)) columns. Default integer and real sp/dp/qp variants are exposed. This supports the N8 permuting leaf, independently of how the permutation was obtained. The caller must supply valid indices with the correct direction; the inspected bodies do not validate a bijection or compute its inverse.
